543929|2026-09.headline: HMA Agro Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 17.7% YoY to INR 2,733.11 crore, with EBITDA up 70.56% YoY to INR 130.35 crore.
543929|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR 2,733.11 crore, up about 17.7% YoY and 31.9% QoQ, while standalone EBITDA rose to INR 130.35 crore with margin at 4.51%. Consolidated revenue was INR 2,779.48 crore (up about 29% YoY), but consolidated EBITDA margin of 5.25% was below the 6.10% of Q2 FY26. Management attributed growth to both volume and realisation gains, citing higher freight and handling costs passed on to buyers. Management said it does not need major capex now, with plant utilisation at about 65-70%. The call was largely Q&A from individual investors, and several figures were deferred to email follow-up.

segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 2,779.48 crore, EBITDA INR 153.54 crore (5.25% margin) and PAT INR 104.57 crore; margin trails last year's 6.10% despite higher revenue.

Management expects demand growth to continue, citing buyers stocking food amid global uncertainty and Indian product price competitiveness.

demand_pricing: Clientele spans about 49 countries across four continents; growth cited from Southeast Asia, South Africa, and GCC.

Rice and seafood are early-stage categories; the company did not disclose their revenue contribution on the call.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company protecting margins against elevated logistics costs, and how will profitability evolve as costs normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said freight rose from about 6x to 10x and is at a peak; lower freight would help margins because buyers already pay current prices. It estimated recovering half of normal freight could add 1.5-2% to margins.

qa_highlights.question: Which new markets or geographies offer growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Southeast Asia, South Africa and GCC were cited as growing; Egypt, Vietnam, Malaysia and Indonesia were named as buyers of buffalo meat.

qa_highlights.question: Can volumes scale through better capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current utilisation is about 65-70%, so the existing plant can take more orders without major new capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mix of volume versus value in recent revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth came from both volume and realisation, with higher logistics and handling costs passed through. It did not give an average price figure.

qa_highlights.question: What capex or new geographies are planned, and what drove the other-expenses reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: No large capex is planned; only working capital for more orders and routine small machines. Management will follow up by email on routine capex and the other-expenses decline.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from other categories and what is the NOP sales contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose these figures on the call and said they would be shared by email.

risks_watch: Freight and logistics costs remain volatile due to Middle East tensions and crude oil; any further rate increase would pressure margins.
Consolidated EBITDA margin (5.25%) is below last year's 6.10%, and consolidated PAT margin (3.76%) is below 4.17% a year ago.
Working capital needs may rise with order growth, as capex is minimal.
Undisclosed figures to watch: revenue split for chilled meat, seafood, rice and fruits, the NOP sales share, and the sources of the other-expenses reduction.

543931|2026-03.headline: Veefin standalone FY26 operating revenue rose ~90% to INR 70.74 crore, with EBITDA margin at 53.89%; qualified pipeline is ~$80 million.
543931|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as a year of scale and platform build-out, positioning Veefin as a multi-product BFSI tech platform rather than a supply-chain finance (SCF) company. Standalone operating revenue rose from INR 37.32 crore to INR 70.74 crore, EBITDA margin expanded ~800 bps to 53.89%, and diluted EPS was INR 7 (up ~50%), while PAT margin fell on higher depreciation and finance costs. The management-view perimeter (Veefin Solutions, Estorifi, GlobeTF) reported INR 91.75 crore revenue and INR 44.7 crore EBITDA (48.7% margin). Management said FY27 will focus on execution, monetisation and conversion of the pipeline, with new product capex lower than FY26.

financial_highlights.change: PAT margin lower YoY on depreciation and finance costs

after adding ~INR 253 crore from other group/service entities
Veefin product-level capex INR 107 crore; INR 130 crore on standalone-plus-perimeter basis

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 91.75 crore, EBITDA INR 44.7 crore (48.7% margin), PAT INR 23.6 crore. Management intends to use this perimeter as the reporting lens after the amalgamation, which is with NCLT.

Pricing 65 bps, of which 15 bps covers onboarding manpower on Veefin's payroll (26 locations).

qa_highlights.question: What success ratio should be expected from the bid pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said conversion is much higher than one-third; at least 25% of the pipeline should convert over the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: What will promoter shareholding be post-merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter holding will be 30% after the merger, rising to 39.41% once all warrants are exercised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PSB Xchange transacted volume and ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the platform is at the approvals stage; limit distribution to suppliers and dealers has started, so financing requests should show up in the current quarter. No transaction value was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY26 and FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was INR 107 crore at product level, INR 130 crore perimeter, INR 187 crore consolidated. FY27 capex will be lower than FY26; no number given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7-year PSB Xchange exclusivity live and how is onboarding staffed?
qa_highlights.answer: Exclusivity started with the first bank onboarding. Onboarding staff are on Veefin's payroll across 26 locations, and banks are also using them for off-platform business.

qa_highlights.answer: DSO improved to 99 days from ~130. Short-term borrowings rose because long-term debt due this year was reclassified; long-term debt relates to the White Rivers acquisition and is backed by FDs.

qa_highlights.answer: Securitisation has been put on the back burner given the macro environment. Epikindifi is in arbitration over governance; it contributed under 2% of consolidated numbers and was loss-making.

543931|2026-06.headline: Veefin standalone Q1 FY27 revenue rose 128% YoY to Rs 23.14 crore, with EBITDA at Rs 12.83 crore (55.4% margin) and PAT at Rs 6.74 crore.
543931|2026-06.overview: Management reported standalone revenue of Rs 23.14 crore (up 128% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 12.83 crore at a 55.4% margin, and PAT of Rs 6.74 crore (up 151% YoY). Consolidated revenue was Rs 113.97 crore with PAT of Rs 9.5 crore, which management said reflects the group perimeter rather than margin deterioration. Five new clients were signed, including a six-product win with a GCC digital bank, and the qualified pipeline ended the quarter at about $80 million after $15.27 million converted. The amalgamation is at step five of seven, with the NCLT second motion petition being filed. Management also disclosed Rs 50 crore of short-term debt at roughly 14-15%, secured by promoter share pledges, to bridge working capital.

segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 23.14 crore, EBITDA Rs 12.83 crore (55.4%), PAT Rs 6.74 crore; management says this is the purest view of product economics. Revenue split roughly 50-50 domestic and international.

segments.name: Consolidated (statutory perimeter, incl. subsidiaries and group entities)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 113.97 crore, EBITDA Rs 22.4 crore (19.7%), PAT Rs 9.5 crore (8.3%). Management attributes the lower margin to subsidiaries' different business profile, not deterioration.

guidance_outlook: Management says FY27 is the year the platform shifts from building to monetising; amalgamation expected to close within the next quarter to quarter and a half, with NCLT final order as the last substantive step.
Revenue from signed deals to be recognised as implementation fees over roughly 9 months, then licence fees from go-live, and AMC from year 2; all five Q1 contracts are five-year terms.
Services EBITDA margin (about 20%) expected to remain similar over the next 3-5 years, per management.
Half-yearly numbers to show TREDX platform revenue, as payment milestones for signed trade and cash deals fall in later periods.
Management plans to retire the short-term debt (2-3 year tenure) earlier than maturity.
capex_capacity: Management said the capex cycle this year is much lower than last year, but working capital needs remain because revenue is lumpy while spend is roughly constant through the year.
PSB Xchange: 3 lenders live, 7 under integration (about half non-PSU), 22 yet to start; 10 lenders now presented deals (3 live plus 7 in progress).
PSB Xchange limits increased to Rs 5,800 crore from Rs 5,400 crore; cumulative requirements rose to Rs 26,000 crore; 94 corporate deals in the pipeline at some stage.
Management sees an inflection point at 10-12 integrated banks, when inter-bank competition starts.
demand_pricing: Qualified pipeline bridge: opened at $79.62 million, added $20.4 million, converted $15.27 million, and removed about $4.5 million deferred on timelines; closed at $80.13 million.
Pipeline mix: about 70% non-supply-chain finance and about 70% outside India; 26 of 52 tracked deals involve more than one product.

Five new clients signed in Q1, including a six-product win with a large GCC digital bank (LOS, LMS, collections, trade finance, supply chain, limits microservice) and a Middle East non-bank lender taking LOS, LMS and collections; a five-country Africa supply chain and LOS rollout.
Pipeline and deal values are stated as five-year contract value (implementation, licence and AMC fees combined).
Management says Veefin wins on technology architecture but falls short against incumbents with 30-40 year histories.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise debt at 15-16% when equity is cheaper, and why is Rs 50 crore needed if capex is falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited equity market timing, permanent dilution, and the view that the stock price is not attractive. Promoters pledged shares to secure the debt. The debt is for working capital gaps from lumpy revenue, with plans to retire it over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Is pipeline stalling, given it moved only from Rs 79.62 crore to Rs 80.13 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said $15.27 million was converted and $20.4 million added, replenishing about 25% of the opening pipeline in one quarter. It acknowledged the replenishment should ideally have been slightly lower.

qa_highlights.question: Why are only 3 of 32 lender integrations live?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed delays to lender IT bandwidth and PSU legacy systems, and said non-PSU lenders make up about half of the 7 integrations in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What triggers invocation of the promoter pledge, and what happens if the NCLT approval slips?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pledge is not price-linked. The covenants are EBITDA at most 3x and DSCR at least 1.25, with headroom described as large. Management does not expect NCLT delay; if it slips by months, it is outside company control.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Rs 60 crore subsidiary debts, and did standalone guarantee them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 60 crore sits with subsidiaries Infini and Nityo, and that Veefin (standalone) has provided guarantees for it.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PSB Xchange pipeline Rs 26,000 crore while approvals are Rs 5,800 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said banks set their own pace; the platform surfaces requests to providers but cannot accelerate bank decisions. Competition among banks is expected once 10-12 are integrated.

543931|2026-09.headline: Veefin H1 FY27 group revenue rose 116.2% to Rs 238.82 crore, with group PAT of Rs 24.85 crore and a 25.5% EBITDA margin.
543931|2026-09.overview: Group revenue for H1 FY27 was Rs 238.82 crore, up 116.2% YoY, with group EBITDA of Rs 60.81 crore (25.5% margin) and PAT of Rs 24.85 crore (10.4% margin). Q2 revenue rose 9.2% QoQ to Rs 124.66 crore, and Q2 EBITDA margin was 29.4% versus 21.1% in Q1. Management reported an open pipeline of about Rs 920 crore with Rs 240 crore added in Q2, a new AI operating system (AIOS), and senior hires in delivery and customer roles. Operating cash flow was negative in H1, which management attributed to timing of billing and collections, and it expects H2 to improve.

segments.name: Standalone revenue mix
segments.commentary: Recurring fees were 82.1% of standalone H1 revenue and 89.8% in Q2. Existing customers contributed 73.9% of H1 revenue and 69.9% of Q2 revenue.

segments.name: Opportunity pipeline by product
segments.commentary: Supply chain finance about 35% of pipeline value, digital lending about 23%, trade and cash about 18%, digital banking about 16%, and fraud and risk in single digits. Geographically, about 84% is outside India (Southeast Asia, Middle East, Africa) and 16% in India.

segments.name: Subsidiary: White Rivers Media
segments.commentary: Consolidated for six months in H1 FY27 versus three months in H1 FY26, which management cited as a reason for the rise in cost of revenue. A DRHP listing filing is expected in January.

guidance_outlook: Management stated its EBITDA margin guidance range is 45% to 50%, and it is currently tracking above that range.
Management said it would not give formal forward guidance but expects its current revenue growth rate to continue for the next two years.
Management said product development spend is at the end of its cycle, and from next year essentially 99% will flow through the P&L rather than the balance sheet.
Management said no fresh debt or equity raise is planned; only already-sanctioned working capital lines will be drawn.
H2 is expected to be stronger on billing and collections, which management expects to reverse the H1 negative operating cash flow on a full-year basis.
capex_capacity: Veefin AIOS (AI operating system) has more than 1,000 reusable skills built, and three internal factories (implementation, support and testing) are running on it.
BSE in-principle approval for migration to the main board is in place; the NSE application is pending.
Voluntary adoption of Ind AS was made in preparation for the main board move, with restatement of past financials.

543942|2026-03.headline: Utkarsh SFB posted a net loss of INR188 crores in Q4 FY26 on legacy MFI provisioning, while GNPA fell ~330 bps QoQ to 7.7%.

Management is shifting the mix toward secured lending (51% of gross loans) and reducing JLG exposure (~28% of gross loans). qa_highlights.question: What is the planned JLG portfolio run-down and the overall growth outlook for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects JLG to hold around 25% of the book over the next 2-3 years, with Micro Banking plus business loans growing 15-20%, overall loan growth 25-30%, and JLG growth below 20%. Sarjukumar said the book will keep growing rather than run down, with the JLG/Micro Banking cap around 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost and NPA guidance applies for the rest of FY27, and are further fundraises planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost guided at the upper end of 3-3.5%, described as conservative. The INR500 crore Tier 2 NCD adds about 250 bps to CRAR, while the INR195 crore 12.5% tranche is being redeemed early in mid-August, saving about INR20 crore. No equity raise is expected until at least end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the asset quality of the post-guardrail book and how is CGFMU coverage positioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Post-April 2025 book is the majority of outstanding JLG book with GNPA of about 1.85-1.9%. CGFMU coverage is 60% for disbursements up to Q4 FY26 and about 80% including Q1 FY27 disbursements.

qa_highlights.question: How is MBBL sourced and underwritten, and is it going to new-to-bank customers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 99.9% of MBBL is existing customers with 2-3 prior cycles; new-to-bank is a small pilot of no more than about 100-200 accounts. MBBL outstanding is about INR2,246 crore, of which INR2,036 crore is post April 2025, with only 0.3% NPA in that pool. A separate underwriting team and a dedicated MBBL collection team are used.

qa_highlights.question: Why are recoveries slow, and how much of the slippage/NPA pool is in Micro Banking?
qa_highlights.answer: Slow retail recoveries are due to SARFAESI-linked legacy cases, with processes taking 6-7 months to auction. About INR28 crore of the recoveries pool was from Micro Banking. Recoveries are expected to pick up in Q2 and Q3, with about 1,100 JLG collection staff being redeployed to recoveries and write-offs.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the growth guidance given weak Q1 growth and how credible is it?

qa_highlights.question: Why is PPOP growing slowly and what is the path to profitability and cost-to-income?
qa_highlights.answer: PPOP moved from negative about INR44 crore in December to INR12 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR64 crore in Q1 FY27. Management expects cost-to-income to improve as income recovers with flat costs, with 2-digit ROE exiting FY27 and about 15% ROE in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank keep growing microfinance, and what is the risk weight on incremental MFI loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will keep MFI at about 25% of the book. Under CGFMU, only about INR15 of every INR100 of incremental MFI book gets zero risk weight, because the benefit is capped at 15% of crystallised disbursements; the remaining INR85 carries risk weight.

543957|2026-09.headline: Redtape Q2 FY27 revenue fell 3.5% YoY to INR 474 crores on Big Billion Days shift, but EBITDA margin rose 204 bps to 18.9% and PAT grew 27.3%.
543957|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 474 crores, down 3.5% YoY, which management attributed mainly to Big Billion Days moving from September to October, shifting sales into Q3. Profitability improved: gross margin rose to 45.4%, EBITDA grew 8.2% to INR 89 crores (margin 18.9%, up 204 bps), and PAT grew 27.3% to INR 36 crores. For H1, revenue was broadly flat at INR 955 crores, with EBITDA up 12.4% and PAT up 22.7%. Online share recovered to about 31% of revenue from about 22% in Q1, and the brand website sales reached INR 31.9 crores versus INR 3.9 crores a year earlier.

segments.commentary: Footwear accounted for 63% of Q2 revenue. Apparel and accessories are being built on shared sourcing, merchandising and distribution. No separate segment figures were given.

H2 focus: stronger profitability, balanced online mix, website growth, retail productivity, and discipline on pricing and margins.

Stores are COCO, franchise (FOFO), and a few company-owned stores run by third-party staff management. Historically online is about 30% and retail about 70% of revenue.

543959|2026-03.headline: SBFC Q4 FY26: AUM up 29% YoY to INR 11,270 crore, PAT up 30% to INR 123 crore, credit cost steady at 1.38%.
543959|2026-03.overview: SBFC reported Q4 FY26 AUM of INR 11,270 crore, up 29% YoY and 8% QoQ, with gold loans reaching 21% of the book. Spreads widened 56 bps YoY to 9.09% as cost of borrowing fell 83 bps to 8.52%, and opex fell 69 bps YoY to 3.93%. PAT rose 30% YoY to INR 123 crore, with FY26 PAT at INR 451 crore (+31%). Management kept FY27 guidance broadly unchanged: 5-7% quarterly growth, flat spreads, opex down 20-25 bps and credit cost range-bound around 1.38%. Branch count reached 251 with a plan to stabilise near 275.

qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said upfront investment in state, regional and supervisor layers is already in place, so incremental cost is mainly front-end staff at low unit cost; opex is still guided down 20-25 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Will SBFC need DSAs or connectors to sustain growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said the current distribution can deliver about 20% disbursal growth next year, with no need for indirect channels for at least two years.

qa_highlights.question: Sensitivity of growth and gold mix to gold prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said gold growth is mostly price-driven; FY27 gold growth is pencilled in on full-year benefit from branches added in FY26, not on higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is credit cost guidance conservative given early delinquency improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said guidance is cautious given the macro (fuel, rainfall, heat); April numbers show no stress in LPG- and fertiliser-linked sectors.

qa_highlights.question: Path to ROE of 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said ROE is an outcome of ROA and leverage (about 4.57% ROA, 3.17x leverage, ~14.5% ROE); management called 18% optimistic and cited more than 15% ROE on 25% growth if ROA compresses about 25 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ARC sell-down a driver of reported GNPA?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said ARC sales are used to clean up hard-to-collect assets and recoveries under SARFAESI; benefits flow to P&L. No extra provision overlay was held beyond the March model refresh.

Credit cost guided flat at 1.38% while stage 2 rose from about 6% to 16% (per Mahesh Dayani); watch slippage and 1+ DPD (benchmarked 7-9%).

Rating upgrade is possible but not guided; management declined to comment.

543959|2026-06.headline: SBFC Q1 FY27: PAT rose 29% YoY to INR 130 crores and spreads widened 39 bps QoQ to 9.48%, while 0+ DPD rose 70 bps and AUM grew 6% QoQ.
543959|2026-06.overview: AUM reached INR 11,922 crores (up 27% YoY, 6% QoQ), with MSME AUM at INR 9,271 crores and gold loan AUM at INR 2,631 crores. Spreads improved to 9.48% and NIM to 10.6%, helped by a 90 bps YoY drop in cost of borrowing to 8.42%. Management cited headwinds: lower gold-loan eligibility after April 1, 2026 rules, a regulatory cap on bank collateral for sub-20 lakh MSME tickets that hit co-origination, and softer login-to-disbursal conversion (34% vs 42%). Asset quality weakened QoQ, with 0+ DPD up 70 bps and GNPA at 2.66%, but Stage 2 ECL was raised to 16% from 6% and total provisioning reached 1.91% of assets.

segments.commentary: MSME AUM INR 9,271 crores (+4.5% QoQ) and disbursements INR 809 crores (+3% QoQ). Co-origination, about 20% of disbursals and book, reset to about 10% after RBI collateral rule for sub-20 lakh MSME tickets; management expects a return to usual run rate from this quarter.

segments.name: Gold loan
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2,631 crores (+11% QoQ). Gold yields rose in the quarter and were the main driver of the 29 bps QoQ yield increase; management expects gold yields to stay range-bound, with at most a marginal decline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for incremental yield and gold yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental yield is in the same 17.50%-17.75% range, slightly up because of gold. Gold yields are expected to be range-bound with at most a marginal fall; the recent 25-30 bps rise should not be extrapolated.

risks_watch: Sub-10 lakh household segment: management says conditions have not improved, CLSA household DSR near 14%, and the company cannot tell whether the cycle is early or mid; watch the disbursal mix and ticket size there.
Asset quality: 0+ DPD rose 70 bps QoQ and management called it homework for the current quarter, expecting stabilisation this quarter and rollbacks in later quarters; GNPA 2.66%.
Co-origination recovery: management expects co-origination to return to its usual run rate this quarter after the RBI collateral rule cut its share to about 10%; verify in Q2 disbursals.
Cost to AUM: opex 4.29% needs to fall to about 4% or below by year-end as branches opened in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 mature; employee cost stays elevated in the near term.
Funding and rates: management flagged an upward bias in Indian interest rates from crude above $100 and deposit rates, while saying cost of borrowing should now stabilise at current levels.
Gold yields: management says the 25-30 bps rise should not be extrapolated and gold yields may drift marginally lower; spread floor of 9% depends on holding yields at 17.50%-17.75%.
key_quotes: We'd rather over-insulate the P&L now than explain a surprise later, call it prudence with a margin of safety.
So, we don't want to, at this stage look at anything different or new.
But I think the only parameter that one should probably look at is whether we've been able to maintain our spreads.
My sense is that the 25-30 basis increase you shouldn't pencil-in and extrapolate the numbers from here.
543959|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on spreads, NIM, PAT and provisioning, with a cautious tone on the household segment and on macro, rates and oil. Management repeatedly stressed that guidance is unchanged and that it would rather slow growth than push loans that fail screens.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Spread at 9.48% (+39 bps QoQ) and management guides spreads above 9% with yield at 17.50%-17.75%, but gold yield gains are not to be extrapolated and cost of borrowing is stable at 8.42%; opex/AUM at 4.29% must fall about 25 bps in FY27 to ~4% by year-end as Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 branches mature.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch count 256 after 5 added in Q1, with 10-15 more planned in FY27; this is a modest, profitability-gated addition, not a major capacity step-up.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM 11,922 crores (+6% QoQ, +27% YoY) with a path to 15,000 crores, but login-to-disbursal conversion fell to 34% from 42%, about 1,400 applications per quarter (~INR 140 crores of disbursals) failed filters, and management will not push weak loans.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says it will 'go slow' with 10-15 branches in FY27 and gates expansion on the profitability of recent branches; no utilisation or capacity constraint is cited and liquidity is being built up instead.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says guidance is unchanged and it would rather slow growth than push loans that fail screens; the household segment is still stressed with no sign of improvement.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: 0+ DPD rose 70 bps QoQ, GNPA is 2.66%, and credit cost of 1.45% sits at the top of the 1.4-1.5% range, with the sub-10 lakh household segment stressed and rate risk from crude above $100.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said it will focus on the existing two products (small-ticket LAP and gold loans) and sees no need for new products or geographies to meet FY27 guidance.

rows.label: Co-origination recovery to usual run rate
rows.why: Co-origination was reset to about 10% of disbursals and book (from about 20%) after the RBI collateral rule for sub-20 lakh tickets; management expects a return to normal run rate this quarter, which is not yet proven.

rows.label: Gold-loan eligibility reset and falling gold prices
rows.why: Eligibility norms reset from April 1, 2026 and falling gold prices reduced loan amounts reaching customers, though gold AUM still grew 11% QoQ to INR 2,631 crores and gold yields are expected to stay range-bound.

rows.label: Opex/AUM down 25 bps in FY27 to about 4%
rows.why: Opex/AUM was 4.29% (+36 bps QoQ); management reiterated the 25 bps FY27 reduction as Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 branches mature over the next nine months.

tone.note: Management was confident on spreads, PAT and provisioning and kept guidance unchanged, but cautious on the sub-10 lakh household segment, rates and crude; analysts pressed on the household credit cycle, product expansion and whether yield gains were driven by riskier lending.

543959|2026-09.headline: SBFC Q2 FY27 PAT rose 27% YoY to INR 139 crore, with ROE at 15.04% and AUM up 27% YoY to INR 12,592 crore.
543959|2026-09.overview: SBFC reported its 36th consecutive quarter of sequential AUM and profit growth, with AUM at INR 12,592 crore (up 6% QoQ, 27% YoY) and PAT of INR 139 crore (up 7% QoQ, 27% YoY). Credit cost eased to 1.37% from 1.44% and Opex fell to 4.07%, while spreads widened to 9.63%. Management said the gold-loan delinquency rise after the RBI circular was the main source of higher Stage 2 assets, and that the MSME book has stabilised rather than improved. Management kept its 5-7% quarterly AUM growth guidance and warned against treating 9.6% spreads as a new norm.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME AUM INR 9,669 crore (77% of AUM), up 18% YoY and 4.3% QoQ; on-book grew 20% and co-origination 10%. MSME disbursements INR 855 crore, up 6% QoQ, the third straight quarter of growth.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan AUM INR 2,906 crore (about 23% of AUM); added INR 275 crore in Q2, roughly INR 40 lakh net growth per branch per month across 236 gold branches. Management is deliberately cautious on volume and LTV expansion.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 5-7% per quarter going forward; management said MSME disbursements should grow in double digits second-half over second-half.
Opex expected to fall by a further 25 bps in FY27, with a further reduction over the next two quarters.
Spread guided around 9-9.25%, but management asked investors not to model 9.6% as the norm due to rising gold competition and likely pricing rationalisation.
Credit cost seen stabilising at around 1.37% or marginally lower unless El Nino or state waivers materially change the outlook; 1.45% in Q1 described as likely peak.
Capital sufficient to an AUM of about INR 20,000 crore before the next capital raise; ROE expansion expected as leverage rises.
PLR raised 25 bps in October 2026; management expects spreads to hold as variable-rate MSME assets reprice.
CARE and India Ratings revised outlook from stable to positive.
capex_capacity: Branch count 257 as of September 2026 (1 added in Q2, 6 in H1); 236 branches do gold loans.
Collection team about 850 including supervisors (about 700 front-end), up 150-200 in the period.
LCR at 194%; closing liquidity INR 1,782 crore in Q2 versus INR 1,864 crore in Q1.
AI voice ran the first full pre-due collection cycle in October: more than 4 lakh calls to 35,000 accounts, 84% reached, 53% paid, replacing roughly a 60-person team.
demand_pricing: Banks are moving to higher-ticket prime borrowers at single-digit pricing, leaving INR 10-25 lakh and INR 25+ lakh MSME segments with headroom for SBFC.
Sub-INR 7 lakh book is being run down and is no longer originated; it is under 6% of AUM per management.
Gold competition rising as large players open branches; gold yields range 18-21%, with management expecting roughly 23% and possibly 25%.
Co-origination rose to INR 112 crore from INR 78 crore in Q1.
Management expects MSME disbursements to stabilise and grow; Q2 was the highest disbursement level in the MSME business since listing per management.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan stress and how the industry is positioned, given larger players entering gold.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not chase high-volume gold growth, as it expects pricing to be compromised; it said gold yields are 18-21% and competition has risen in the last 1-1.5 months, with some large players opening 500-1,000 branches.

qa_highlights.question: Why slippages (GS2+GS3) rose QoQ, and whether the ARC sale was gold or MSME.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise in Stage 2 is entirely from gold loans after the RBI circular reset scheme design, as customers move from bullet to monthly interest payments. The ARC sale was a lower-ticket vintage LAP portfolio; no gold loans were sold.

qa_highlights.question: Gold price sensitivity and LTV risk.
qa_highlights.answer: LTV fell to 67% from about 70% last quarter (versus about 60s in June 2025). Auctions are triggered after 85-90% LTV and delinquency, with a 7-30 day window per management; out-of-money risk described as not significant.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of MSME disbursement pick-up.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the repositioning is done and restaffing is complete in most locations; it expects second-half over second-half disbursement growth of at least double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state 0+ DPD and credit cost.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 0+ rose from around 7% to above 9% and is now stabilising; it expects 0+ to hold in the 8-9.2% range, not return to 7%, and credit cost to stabilise near 1.37%.

qa_highlights.question: Whether 4.5% ROA can be sustained as guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROA has held above 4.5% for 7-8 quarters despite higher leverage; holding 4.6% over the long run will be difficult, but it should hold in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: Collection headcount and bandwidth.
qa_highlights.answer: About 700 front-end collectors and 850 including supervisors; average caseload of 40-45 per collector, varying from 25-30 in Assam to about 50 in South India.

risks_watch: Gold: competitive pricing pressure, possible yield compression, and a possible fall in gold prices (LTV fell to 67%; October saw a drop).
El Nino and drought: rainfall deficit concentrated in Karnataka and Maharashtra; state-level waivers could affect repayment behaviour.
Rising rates: 25 bps repo hike and cost of funds expected to rise; management expects spreads to hold, but pass-through of MCLR-linked debt is still to come.
Draft regulatory circular that management said may affect profitability.
Stage 2 and 0+ DPD trends, with 0+ above 9% versus about 7% historically; track whether they keep stabilising in Q3.
543959|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics and conservative in outlook: management stressed consistency and 'boring' results, repeatedly cautioned on gold and macro risk, and said asset quality has stabilised rather than improved. It was evasive on the precise gold-loan granularity an analyst asked for, promising to consider adding it to future presentations.
key_quotes: We are building SBFC to deliver consistent quarterly performance despite the noise.
Please do not pencil in 9.6% in your models as the new norm, since competitive intensity in gold is rising and some pricing rationalization is likely.
So to say that will it go below 7% will be a tall ask. We don't think it will reach there.
In our case, we've been able to hold on to more than 4.5% ROA for now more than 7 - 8 quarters despite increase in leverage.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Spread guided at 9-9.25% versus 9.63% in Q2 and management asked not to model 9.6% as the norm; opex to AUM down 22 bps QoQ to 4.07% with a further 25 bps FY27 reduction guided, but credit cost is seen flat at about 1.37%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Only 1 branch added in Q2 (257 total, 6 in H1) and no further openings quantified; capital is sufficient to about INR 20,000 crore AUM versus INR 12,592 crore today.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM guided at 5-7% per quarter (about 22-32% annualised) versus 27% YoY now; MSME disbursements at INR 855 crore, third straight quarter of growth, with second-half over second-half growth guided at double digits.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capital is sufficient to about INR 20,000 crore AUM before the next raise, against INR 12,592 crore today, and no new capex was discussed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held AUM and opex guidance and warned against treating 9.6% spreads as the norm, pointing to spread compression rather than an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gold competition rising with yields at 18-21%, possible pricing rationalisation, and 0+ DPD at above 9% versus about 7% historically could pull spreads or credit cost off guidance.

rows.label: Draft regulatory circular may affect profitability
rows.why: Management flagged a draft regulatory circular it said may affect profitability, with no quantified impact given.

rows.label: Gold pricing pressure from large entrants
rows.why: Large players opening 500-1,000 branches each and gold yields at 18-21%, with management expecting pricing to be compromised; SBFC is choosing not to chase gold volume.

rows.label: Banks retreating to prime segments
rows.why: Banks moving to higher-ticket prime borrowers at single-digit pricing leave INR 10-25 lakh and INR 25+ lakh MSME segments open, supporting MSME disbursement growth.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating metrics and held AUM and opex guidance but cautious on gold competition, 0+ DPD above 9%, and spread normalisation; analysts pushed on gold-loan granularity and slippage drivers, which management answered only partly.

543960|2026-03.headline: Concord Biotech FY26 revenue fell 12% to a level where API sales were INR 829 crores, with management guiding to growth slightly above its ~18% historical rate in FY27.
543960|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: revenue declined about 12% and Q4 revenue fell 24% YoY, driven by a roughly three-month CDSCO-related halt in European supplies, a Middle East tender held in abeyance, and a US Veterans Affairs tender on hold. Management attributes the shortfall to timing rather than demand, pricing or market share loss, and says deferred volumes are spilling into FY27. Profitability held up better than revenue: reported FY26 EBITDA was INR 367 crores at about 35%, and PAT fell 30% to INR 260 crores. The company remains debt-free with over INR 414 crores of cash.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: FY26 API revenue INR 829 crores (-12%); Q4 INR 264 crores (-27%). Management said there was no price growth and the decline was volume-driven. Anti-infectives and oncology are expected to grow faster than immunosuppressants in FY27.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue fell about 13% in FY26 and 8% in Q4, mainly from the European halt and Middle East formulation tender. Management says the domestic and US formulation businesses grew.

segments.name: Injectables (new facility)
segments.commentary: Expenses of about INR 38-39 crores in FY26 (about INR 10 crores per quarter). WHO-GMP certified; filings are under way with Southeast Asia and Africa as first targets. Management said full breakeven is more likely in FY27.

segments.name: Stellon Biotech (US subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Set up in FY26 with licences for direct US marketing. Management expects first supplies in H1 FY27 with orders already in place, and expenses were fully booked in FY26.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Management classes only third-party IP work as CDMO; it expects 1-4% of FY26 revenue, with one advanced-stage opportunity that could change this.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth expected to be slightly better than the historical ~18% rate, with visibility in H1 and growth expected from Q1-Q2.
No formal EBITDA margin guidance. Management cited a 1-1.5% EBITDA tailwind from solar/renewable power, partly offset by higher LPG and furnace oil costs.
Gross margin expected to be in a similar range to historical levels for the full year.
API:formulation mix expected around 80:20 with a plus or minus 2-3% range.
Capex guided at INR 20-30 crores per year maintenance. A smaller topical facility may come in FY27; larger capex only for new customer projects.
Working capital intensity expected to be in line with historical levels; inventory days should normalise in FY27 H1.
capex_capacity: Unit 1 is at optimal utilisation at 77%; Unit 2 at 30%; Unit 3 at about 53% (close to 50%).
Unit 4 expected to reach breakeven by next year.
Four units support peak revenue potential of about INR 3,000 crores.
FY26 capex of INR 65 crores included the soft gel facility and modifications for a larger-volume innovator project; CWIP is INR 79.3 crores.
Management expects another INR 50-100 crore capex cycle in 2-3 years and anything above INR 100 crores in 4-5 years.
demand_pricing: Customers shifted from bulk buying to staggered quarterly procurement in H2 FY26, pushing revenue into later quarters.
Management says there is no pricing pressure on new second-source launches (Nystatin, Fusidic Acid); some mature products face price pressure from certain customers, offset by new regions.
Middle East exposure is about INR 50 crores at company level. The major tender was about INR 25 crores (formulation) and remains in abeyance; API supplies to the region are gradually resuming.
US Veterans Affairs tender not finalised and remains on hold; exposure was about INR 25 crores.
Fuel supply shortages in April 2026 were resolved, but LPG and furnace oil prices remain higher; about 10% of total costs are LPG or furnace oil based.
Commenced supplies of APIs to 2 innovator companies; 2 CDMO opportunities in discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Is there visibility on FY27 growth starting in H1, and what size is the growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is a fair amount of visibility in H1 and expects FY27 growth slightly better than the historical ~18%, starting from Q1-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East exposure and tender size?
qa_highlights.answer: The tender was about INR 25 crores, mostly formulation. Total current Middle East exposure is about INR 50 crores at company level, with API supplies gradually building up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the contribution of the injectable and Stellon losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Injectable expenses were about INR 38-39 crores for FY26, roughly INR 10 crores a quarter. Stellon costs were fully booked in FY26; management said full breakeven for both is more likely in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise to 480 from 286?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited staggered customer procurement, shipments pushed into Q1-Q2 FY27, and higher fermentation utilisation with longer cycles. It expects this to moderate in the first half.

qa_highlights.question: Is the formulation inventory at risk of write-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not hold formulation inventory for the Middle East because of shelf-life issues; inventory is mainly API, so write-off risk is low.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan and CWIP of INR 79.3 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Maintenance capex is INR 20-30 crores a year. CWIP reflects soft gel and modifications for an innovator project; no major growth capex is planned in H1 FY27.

risks_watch: Recovery depends on Middle East tender timing and the geopolitical situation; management said it has no clarity on timing.
US Veterans Affairs tender remains on hold with no timeline.
Injectable and Stellon breakeven timing is uncertain; management declined to quantify.
Inventory days rose to 480 from 286, with INR 326 crore of inventory versus INR 240 crore; the company expects this to normalise in H1 FY27.
Fuel costs (LPG and furnace oil) remain elevated and could offset the 1-1.5% power savings.
CDMO contribution is small (1-4%) and depends on the pending advanced-stage opportunity.
543960|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident about FY27 recovery but cautious on specifics: it declined to give EBITDA guidance or a breakeven date for new units, and repeatedly tied the outlook to H1 visibility. Explanations for the miss were detailed and consistent, though the timing-versus-demand argument rests on deferred volumes that have not yet shown up in revenue.
key_quotes: So we have a very good amount of visibility in the first half.
It is important to note, however, that this was not a case of pent-up demand where all deferred supplies could be immediately executed upon resumption.
The factors mentioned above were largely beyond our control and were not related to lower demand, loss of market share or pricing pressure.
So all the expenses that have been there for these 2 entities have been fully booked in the last financial year.

financial_highlights.value: Q4 FY26 and FY26 degrowth of about 8% and 13% respectively

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin excl. injectable and Stellon costs

financial_highlights.value: More than INR 414 crores at 31 March 2026; zero debt

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management cites a 1-1.5% EBITDA tailwind from solar/renewable power, partly offset by higher LPG and furnace oil costs (about 10% of total costs), and gives no formal EBITDA margin guidance; FY26 EBITDA margin was about 35% reported, about 39-40% excluding injectable and Stellon costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Unit 1 is at 77%, Unit 2 at 30% and Unit 3 at about 53%, so there is spare capacity; the only new facilities (injectables, soft gel) are already commissioned or under construction, and the next INR 50-100 crore capex cycle is 2-3 years out.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 growth slightly above the historical ~18% rate, with visibility in H1 and deferred volumes spilling into FY27 after the three-month CDSCO-related European halt and the Middle East and US VA tenders; Stellon first supplies are expected in H1 FY27 with orders in place, but the revenue timing has not yet shown up.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Maintenance capex is guided at INR 20-30 crore a year, no major growth capex is planned in H1 FY27, and utilisation is well below the 80% threshold (Unit 1 at 77%, Unit 2 at 30%, Unit 3 at 53%).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 growth is guided slightly above ~18%, but that is only an initial guide, and an upgrade depends on Middle East and VA tender timing, which management says it has no clarity on.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY26 revenue fell 12% (Q4 -24%) and the recovery rests on deferred volumes not yet visible in revenue; the Middle East tender is in abeyance (about INR 25 crore), the US VA tender (about INR 25 crore) is on hold with no timeline, and LPG/furnace oil costs remain high.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Stellon Biotech expects first supplies in H1 FY27 with orders in place under direct US marketing licences; injectable filings are under way for Southeast Asia and Africa; second-source launches (Nystatin, Fusidic Acid) and two innovator API supply starts have begun.

rows.label: Injectables and Stellon breakeven in FY27
rows.why: Injectable expenses were about INR 38-39 crore in FY26 (about INR 10 crore a quarter) and Stellon costs were fully booked in FY26; management says full breakeven for both is more likely in FY27 but declined to quantify.

rows.label: Inventory normalisation in H1 FY27
rows.why: Inventory days rose to 480 from 286 and inventory to INR 326 crore from INR 240 crore as shipments were pushed into Q1-Q2 FY27; management expects this to moderate in the first half.

rows.label: No price growth; mature-product price pressure
rows.why: Management says FY26 API decline was volume-driven with no price growth, and some mature products face price pressure from certain customers, offset by new regions and no pricing pressure on Nystatin and Fusidic Acid second-source launches.

tone.note: Management was confident about a FY27 recovery from H1 visibility and deferred volumes, but cautious on specifics: it gave no EBITDA margin guidance, no breakeven date for injectables or Stellon, and no clarity on Middle East or VA tender timing; analysts pushed on the timing-versus-demand argument

543960|2026-06.headline: Concord Biotech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR257 crores, with EBITDA margin at 32% and PAT at INR58 crores.
543960|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached INR257 crores (+26% YoY), led by API at INR219 crores (+42%) while formulations fell 23% to INR39 crores, which management attributed to lost Middle East supplies. Exports grew 46% and domestic grew 12%. EBITDA rose 34% to INR82 crores (32% margin, +190 bps), and gross margin was 78.9%. Management said part of the growth was spillover from Q4 FY26 procurement delays, and that the injectable facility and Stellon Biotech are still at a nascent stage.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Revenue INR219 crores, up 42% YoY. Growth reported across immunosuppressants, anti-infectives, oncology and antifungals; anti-infectives and oncology grew faster than immunosuppressants.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR39 crores, down 23% YoY. Management attributed the decline to Middle East customers buying API instead of formulation in Q1; ex-Middle East, domestic double-digit growth in both Intra (nephrology) and INCA (critical care) divisions.

segments.name: CDMO (fermentation)
segments.commentary: Currently about 1-2% of revenue. One product commercialised in animal health (US, ANDA), currently a couple of million dollars in sales; management aims for double-digit share over time.

segments.name: Injectables
segments.commentary: Facility commercialised; utilisation about 5% in the quarter. Own branded generics supplied in-house; contract manufacturing discussions advanced, with some commercial onboarding expected in 2H FY27. Emerging-market sales expected from next year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects growth in FY27 to exceed the company's historical growth rates, citing visibility for coming quarters.
Spillover from Q4 FY26 procurement delays expected to continue into subsequent quarters; not quantified.
Long-term view: INR3,000 crores revenue from existing infrastructure in about 5-6 years, split roughly INR600-700 crores formulations and INR2,200 crores API.
EBITDA margin expected to exceed sales growth in FY27; 40% margin target expected to be reached partly in FY27 and more fully in FY28, dependent on injectable and Stellon ramp-up.
Two to three new product launches planned annually; a couple of advanced-stage products expected to commercialise in coming quarters.
Injectable facility expected to reach emerging-market sales next year after 12-15 month approval processes.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation: Unit 1 about 80% (analyst later cited 78%); Unit 2 about 25% (analyst later cited 55%); Unit 3 about 55% (includes some KSM manufacturing).
Unit 3 has about 160 acres, with only 20-25% of land used; capacity expansion decision expected at around 80-85% utilisation.
Approximately 1,250 m3 (cited as 1,250-metre cube) fermentation capacity; oncology products run in 5,000-litre fermenters at Unit 1.
Injectable facility: WHO GMP set, validation batches completed, customer audits underway; facility can do close to INR600 crores top line; utilisation about 5%.
Softgel facility added in oral solids; Unit 2 formulation facility at Valthera received NDA Uganda and PPB Kenya inspections; Limbasi facility passed ANVISA inspection.
Possible dedicated fermentation capacity for peptides and veterinary products if growth is needed ahead of the 80-85% threshold.
demand_pricing: Wallet share gains in the quarter were primarily price-driven on existing products, based on economies of scale from fermentation capacity; seeds were sown 8-12 months earlier.
Exports up 46% across Europe, Japan, LatAm and the US; US ANDA approvals received for mycophenolate mofetil and tofacitinib tablets.
Nystatin and fusidic acid (launched FY26, Europe-focused, awaiting CEP) cited as growing products with limited competition.
Management reported no customer concerns on the reported proposed US tariff on generics.
Constant-currency context: USD movement about 10-12% YoY; net impact after input costs about 3-5% flowing to EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How much of growth is normalisation of delayed procurement versus structural gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Some spillover from Q4 FY26 procurement delays contributed; most growth came from new products across all geographies. Similar spillovers are expected in subsequent quarters, though not quantifiable.

qa_highlights.question: Roadmap to INR3,000 crores revenue from existing infrastructure?
qa_highlights.answer: INR600-700 crores from formulations and INR2,200 crores from APIs, expected in about 5-6 years at the current CAGR. Unit 3 has room to expand once utilisation reaches 80-85%.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and CDMO contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 1 about 80%, Unit 3 about 55%, Unit 2 about 25%. CDMO is about 1-2% of revenue, with a target of double digits over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic formulations decline?
qa_highlights.answer: The prior-year quarter included Middle East supplies that did not recur. Ex-Middle East, domestic formulations grew double digits in both divisions.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the wallet share gain attributed to pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing advantage from fermentation scale was passed to customers, and margins were held. Softer factors, such as fermentation partnership, were secondary.

qa_highlights.question: When will the injectable facility reach EBITDA breakeven and emerging-market sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Injectable utilisation is about 5%; breakeven utilisation was not given and will be followed up. Emerging-market sales expected next year after a 12-15 month approval process; contract manufacturing sales expected in 2H FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company reach 40% EBITDA margin by end of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage and renewable energy should drive margins above sales growth. Full 40% depends on injectable and Stellon ramp-up, so it may slip into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How can API revenue reach INR2,200 crores without new capacity, given Unit 1 and Unit 2 utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 3 is the focus for 8-10 pipeline anti-infective and antifungal products. Oncology revenue is high value per litre, so utilisation understates revenue potential. Capacity utilisation for Unit 3 excluding KSMs is slightly above the 20-25% estimate the analyst gave.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin excluding injectable facility and Stellon expenses

financial_highlights.value: More than INR442 crores as on 30 June 2026
About INR9.5 crores in the quarter

543960|2026-09.headline: Concord Biotech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to Rs 309.1 crore, but gross margin fell about 400 bps to 76.2%.
543960|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 25% YoY to Rs 309.1 crore and H1 grew 26% to Rs 566.6 crore, with API up 30% and formulations up 6%. Gross margin contracted about 400 bps to 76.2% on solvent and raw material cost increases, while reported EBITDA margin was 33.8% (33.0% for H1). Management attributed the weak formulation line to customers shifting to buying API and to business moving from Advergent to the US subsidiary Stellon. Injectables (Unit IV) and Stellon are still ramping, and management guided to contract wins in H2 and a 38-40% medium-term EBITDA margin.

543963|2026-03.headline: Shelter Pharma FY26 revenue rose 44% to INR 73.13 Cr with PAT of INR 9.03 Cr; management targets INR 200 Cr revenue by FY2030.
543963|2026-03.overview: Shelter Pharma reported FY26 revenue from operations of INR 73.13 Cr (up 44% YoY), EBITDA of INR 12.72 Cr (margin 17.39%, up 26% YoY) and PAT of INR 9.03 Cr (up 25% YoY). Q4 revenue was INR 39.84 Cr (up 50% YoY) and exports were about INR 6 Cr (up 164%). Management is expanding sales teams and distributors, which has compressed margins from roughly 20-21% in FY24-FY25, and working capital has stretched to 234 days with operating cash flow of minus INR 12.48 Cr. Management reiterated the INR 200 Cr FY2030 revenue target and outlined a second plant near Ahmedabad, with capex of about INR 12-15 Cr.

segments.name: Exports

segments.name: GFS (Global Forwarding Solutions)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 748.8 crore (+34.8% YoY) on India ocean freight volumes; FY26 revenue Rs 2,764.1 crore (+11.4%). Margin 2.4% in Q4 on volume growth and cost actions, but freight rates remain under pressure.

543969|2026-09.headline: Pyramid Technoplast Q2 FY27 revenue up 48% YoY to Rs 238 crore, EBITDA up 61% to Rs 20.3 crore, with EBITDA/ton at Rs 13,718.

H1 revenue rose 42% YoY, while H1 EBITDA margin was about 9%, and management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 15% revenue growth and 11-12% EBITDA margin, including about 1.5 points from subsidy. 543971|2026-03.headline: Bondada guides FY27 revenue growth of 60-70% on a INR7,147 crore order book; FY26 revenue reported at INR2,843 crore.

Q4 EBITDA margin dipped on low-margin billing and higher steel and cable prices, which management says is not structural; FY26 margin rose about 30 bps to 7.5% from 7.2%. Receivable collections from NLC, NTPC, Singareni and MAHAGENCO with working capital of 85-90 days; PSU collection risk not seen.

543972|2026-03.headline: Aeroflex Q4 FY26 total income rose 38% YoY to INR126.5 crore with EBITDA margin of 23.86%; skid assemblies scaling to 15,000 units per annum.

FY26 total income was INR443.3 crore (+17%), EBITDA INR99.7 crore (+26%) and PAT INR55.5 crore. The new liquid cooling skid assemblies business contributed about 5% of FY26 sales, with 617 skids sold, and capacity is being lifted from 6,000 to 15,000 units per annum within about two quarters. Management flagged design and customer quality-audit bottlenecks that delayed skid supply, and guided FY27 growth of about 35% with base business growth of 15-20%.

segments.commentary: Domestic share rose to 31% of FY26 sales from 26%, with domestic sales up about 40% in Q4. Exports still about 60%; exports grew in double digits in Q4 per management. Largest international customer is 25-26% of sales.

543978|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35.46% YoY to ₹387 crores and PAT rose 55.97% to ₹24.07 crores, while the new CCL line remains pre-revenue and guidance is under revision.
543978|2026-09.overview: Ratnaveer reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of ₹387 crores (+35.46% YoY), EBITDA of ₹42.13 crores (+38.85%) and PAT of ₹24.07 crores (+55.97%), which management called the highest in company history. Gross margin dipped to 9.44% in Q2 from 10.33% in Q1, which management attributed to expenses for new products being booked before CCL sales begin. The company is building its first Copper Clad Laminate (CCL) line under the ECMS scheme, targeting trial runs from December 20, 2026 and staged ramp-up across five lines by April 2028. Management said earlier CCL guidance (₹750 crores from five lines, 20% EBITDA, 13% PAT) will be revised soon because CCL prices have risen sharply, but did not give new numbers.

financial_highlights.value: 10.82% (as stated by management); analyst cited 9.4%, management gave gross margin of 9.44%

financial_highlights.metric: Return on equity / Return on capital employed

segments.name: Base business (stainless steel fasteners, clips, washers, tubes and pipes, finishing line, sheet metal)
segments.commentary: Revenue was ₹1,080 crores last year and management expects ₹1,315 crores this year, with a target of ₹1,800 crores by FY28. Finishing line is running near capacity; ₹58 crores of capex this year supports Phase 2 expansion.

segments.name: CCL (Copper Clad Laminate, new line)
segments.commentary: Not yet booking revenue; first line of 15 lakh sheets is targeted to start trial run in December 2026. Planned investment is ₹338 crores over two to three years plus ₹86 crores for a captive solar plant.

guidance_outlook: Earlier CCL guidance (₹750 crores from five lines, 20% EBITDA, 13% PAT) is being kept for now; management said a revised guidance will be announced very soon, with no figures given.
FY28 consolidated targets quoted on old guidance: ₹2,500 crores top line, 14% EBITDA and 11% PAT; management also referred to a 10% consolidated PAT guidance for FY28 and a 13% PAT aspiration.
Full-year FY27 PAT margin expected at around 6.25%; effective tax rate expected near last year's ~15%.
Target of 7-8% share of the Indian CCL market in five years (about 2% today with five lines).
Management said a single CCL line could generate ₹500 crores revenue at current prices, versus ₹150 crores per line in earlier guidance.
capex_capacity: CCL project about 75% complete; civil work almost done. Machinery shipped and expected in India by 15-20 November 2026, with 45-50 days for erection and commissioning.
Trial run targeted 15-20 December 2026 to 20 January 2027, with product run from December 20. Utilisation ramp: 30% in February 2027, 60% by March, 85% by April 2027 (first line).
Line roadmap: line 2 starts June 2027, line 3 September 2027, lines 4 and 5 January and April 2028; orders for lines 2-3 to be placed in December-January.
Chinese team of 22 engineers plus one Chief Technical Officer (30 years' experience) to install machines; one person to stay for two years.
Products: CCL with Tg 140-180, copper thickness 15-35 microns, board thickness 0.8-3.2 mm; FR4 and prepreg, single and double-sided, multi-layer capable.
Phase 2 capex for fasteners, tubes and pipes, sheet metal and clips is ongoing.
demand_pricing: CCL prices have risen by more than 300% over the past year per management, while raw material costs rose 40-50% at most; no Indian CCL producers exist today, and Chinese, Taiwan and Korean suppliers have limited export capacity.

Initial bookings: pricing at par with Chinese imports or 0.5-1% below. Customers get wait-time, logistics, FX and faster delivery benefits. Government offers a 2% incentive to CCL buyers, per management.
Orders received from two companies (Indian PCB makers); long-term contract talks with seven companies. Management expects order confirmations to be announced in about two to three weeks.
Marketing: 57 visits to PCB customers; enquiries from Japan, the US and Europe.
Management expects no competition or anti-dumping duty in the near term; sees the market growing at 50-70% CAGR. Wipro is named as another CCL entrant; Syrma SGS reportedly postponing its CCL plant.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin expected to expand from about 10% to 13%, and what are the volume numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a shift from volume to value and higher CCL margins. Volume figures were not given; revenue was cited instead: ₹1,080 crores last year and ₹1,315 crores this year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the CCL trial timeline and utilisation ramp, and is the 85% target for the first two lines?
qa_highlights.answer: The first line starts trial run 15-20 December; utilisation targets are 30% in February, 60% in March and 85% in April 2027. Line 2 starts June 2027, and all five lines are expected to be installed by April 2028.

qa_highlights.question: How do margins respond to CCL price changes, and what grades are targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CCL prices rose 300%+ on shortage, with raw material up only 40-50%, so PCB makers should pass the increase on. The plant covers Tg 140-180 for PCB, automotive, EV, drone, satellite and aerospace uses.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any anti-dumping duty risk on CCL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no duty is in discussion because there is no domestic producer, so no injury to local industry can exist.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the employee cost low, and when will customer ramp-up happen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of employee cost is capitalised into projects and part is booked as job-work charges, and it is well controlled. Order confirmations and long-term contracts are to be announced in the next couple of weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and cash flow outlook, and are there any commissioning risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rights issue gives enough liquidity for working capital, term loans cover most of the five lines, and a 50% cash subsidy will return part of capex. Operating cash flow is negative only because of capex; no delay is seen, though two to three weeks of teething issues are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall in Q2, and what is the FY27 PAT margin and tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin fell to 9.44% from 10.33% in Q1 because costs for new products were booked before CCL sales. FY27 PAT margin is expected at about 6.25%, with an effective tax rate near last year's ~15%.

risks_watch: CCL commissioning timeline: machines due mid-November, 45-50 days to install, trial run from 15-20 December; any slip pushes revenue beyond FY27.
Revised CCL guidance is promised 'very soon' but no figures were given; the ₹500 crore per-line claim is management's own and unaudited.
Operating cash flow is negative and the new segments have raised inventory and receivables; cash flow improvement depends on capex stabilising.
Gross margin dipped to 9.44% in Q2; new product costs are being expensed before CCL revenue starts.
Order book: no firm CCL order values disclosed; confirmations promised within two to three weeks.
Customer, Chinese-supplier and engineering dependence; a 22-plus-1 person Chinese team is needed for installation.
543978|2026-09.management_tone: Highly confident and promotional on CCL, with repeated forward-looking claims (₹500 crores per line, 300% price rise, 85% utilisation by April 2027). On specifics like new guidance figures, order names, the margin guidance and EBITDA margin drivers, management was evasive and deferred answers to future announcements.
key_quotes: There is a huge margin gap that can open up, and the bottom line can improve drastically.
Very soon we will be present with the new guidance and the revised numbers.
The company has already been receiving orders from two companies.
Once this CapEx stabilises and all the capacities are fully operational, the cash flow will definitely turn positive.

rows.why: Orders for CCL lines 2-3 are to be placed in December-January, Phase 2 capex for fasteners, tubes, sheet metal and clips is ongoing with ₹58 cr this year, and a ₹86 cr captive solar plant is planned alongside the ₹338 cr CCL investment.

rows.why: Management says revised CCL guidance will be announced 'very soon' because CCL prices rose over 300% and it claims ₹500 cr revenue per line vs ₹150 cr in earlier guidance, but no new figures were given and the claim is unaudited.

rows.why: Any slip in the 45-50 day install after mid-November machine arrival would push the 15-20 December trial run and revenue beyond FY27, and Q2 gross margin already dipped to 9.44%.

rows.why: First CCL product (Tg 140-180, 15-35 micron copper, 0.8-3.2 mm board) has a product run from 20 December 2026, with two Indian PCB makers already ordering and seven in long-term contract talks.

rows.why: Orders from two Indian PCB makers received and long-term talks with seven companies, with confirmations promised in about two to three weeks, though no order values were disclosed.

rows.why: Initial bookings priced at par with Chinese imports or 0.5-1% below, with CCL prices up over 300% in a year and raw material up only 40-50%, and no Indian CCL producers exist today.

rows.why: Management says the rights issue funds working capital, term loans cover most of the five lines, and a 50% cash subsidy returns part of capex, though operating cash flow is negative due to capex.

543980|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 15.1% to INR387.8 crores and FY26 total income reached INR1,499.8 crores, with Dombivli opened ahead of schedule.
543980|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR387.8 crores (up 15.1%), EBITDA of INR89.2 crores (23% margin) and PAT of INR50.2 crores (up 11.5%). For FY26, total income was INR1,499.8 crores (up 15.2%), EBITDA INR343.3 crores (up 14.4%, 22.9% margin) and PAT INR194.2 crores. Dombivli, the first greenfield hospital since listing, was inaugurated in February 2026, about two months before the call. Management outlined a pipeline taking capacity from about 1,200 to nearly 3,000 beds, including a 400-bed BKC hospital, with funding planned from internal accruals and debt capped at 3x EBITDA.

segments.name: Thane
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 75%; growth expected to be inflation-linked at current capacity, with an expansion awaiting final approvals.

segments.name: Pune
segments.commentary: Occupancy close to 65% with headroom to grow; Pune South is on track to open in calendar 2028.

segments.name: Indore
segments.commentary: Occupancy 45-50% after last year's added capacity; ramp-up driven by occupancy and case mix; second phase of 111 beds to be triggered when occupancy nears 60%.

segments.name: Dombivli (new, greenfield)
segments.commentary: Opened February 2026 with 750,000 sq ft built, 500-bed superstructure and about 300 beds fitted out; expected EBITDA burn INR2-3 crores per month on average in FY27, with breakeven targeted by end of calendar 2027/2028; INR9.4 crores Dombivli contribution is included in Q4 results.

guidance_outlook: Dombivli: EBITDA burn of INR2-3 crores per month on average for the full year; EBITDA breakeven expected at end of two years of operation (calendar 2027-28).
Dombivli insurance tie-ups expected in 6-12 months, linked to NABH accreditation that needs about six months of operating data.
Pune South to open in calendar 2028; Mira Road expected to start excavation by end of calendar 2026.
Thane expansion approvals expected in FY27; scope and scale to be disclosed once final approvals are received.
Land payment for BKC: 25% of land cost paid; management said the remainder would be paid within this financial year.
Capacity target of about 1,700 new beds in this cycle, taking long-term capacity to nearly 3,000 beds at an average capex of about INR1.5 crores per bed.
Funding: internal accruals over next 4-5 years plus debt capped at 3x EBITDA considered sufficient; detailed calculations to follow.
Base business growth: Thane inflation-linked; Pune inflation plus occupancy; Indore occupancy, inflation and case mix. Management declined to quantify growth given inflation uncertainty.
capex_capacity: Dombivli opened February 2026, ahead of the Q1 FY27 target, on time and on budget with no cost escalation.
BKC: 400-bed quaternary care hospital on over 1 lakh sq ft in BKC; land allotted by MMRDA, with regulatory clearance and possession formalities underway.
Mira Road: architectural drawings complete, regulatory clearances in progress, excavation expected by end of calendar 2026.
Pune South on track for calendar 2028 opening; all projects are greenfield, full-scale hubs in Mumbai and Pune on owned real estate.
Indore phase two (111 beds) on hold until occupancy reaches around 60%.
demand_pricing: ARPOB rose 11.7% YoY to INR67,700 in Q4; drivers cited were Indore case-mix maturity and insurance renewals (roughly every two years) giving price increases plus inflation.
Insurance is 55.4% of revenue; government 1%. Insurance renewals are rolling with no single season.
International medical tourism is very small; management said it is not a focus and is not margin accretive, preferring domestic and local demand within a 45-minute drive radius.
Cost watch items: depreciating rupee and capex cost inflation; doctor costs and consumables not yet materially impacted by global supply chain disruption.
Management referred to a current war situation as a factor limiting inflation visibility.

qa_highlights.question: How is Dombivli ramping in occupancy and revenue, and when will the major insurance tie-up happen?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about two months of operations, so occupancy is too early to quantify; insurance tie-ups are linked to NABH accreditation and are likely in 6-12 months.

qa_highlights.question: How will capex and funding for the expansion to about 2,900 beds be managed over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal accruals over the next 5 years plus some debt, with a self-imposed ceiling of 3x EBITDA, should cover it.

qa_highlights.question: Occupancy and ARPOB by unit, and can the base business grow more than 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Thane about 75% occupancy, Pune close to 65%, Indore 45-50%. Growth is inflation-linked plus occupancy and case mix; no numeric guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ARPOB increase during the year?
qa_highlights.answer: A combination of Indore maturing with better case mix, and insurance renewals after a two-year cycle giving price increases plus inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Will Dombivli add fixed costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, more fixed costs are expected as doctor hiring continues over the next couple of years for a large facility.

qa_highlights.question: Share of revenue from foreign patients and the government's medical tourism push?
qa_highlights.answer: Very little foreign revenue; management is not focused on international medical tourism and does not see it as margin accretive.

risks_watch: Dombivli ramp-up: EBITDA burn of INR2-3 crores per month and rising fixed costs until breakeven; insurance empanelment and NABH accreditation timing.
Funding load from BKC and the wider pipeline (about 1,700 beds, average INR1.5 crores per bed); rupee depreciation and capex cost inflation.
Indore: occupancy still 45-50%, and the second phase depends on occupancy reaching about 60%.
Regulatory approvals for Thane expansion and BKC/Mira Road site clearances (MMRDA possession formalities) remain pending, with no firm dates.
Insurance renewals rolling through the year, with the 55.4% insurance mix exposing the business to tariff negotiations.
Management declined to guide base business growth beyond inflation-linked, citing war-related inflation uncertainty.
543980|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on delivery, citing Dombivli opening early and on budget, but cautious on macro, declining to quantify inflation or base-business growth and deferring capex and occupancy numbers until more data is available.
key_quotes: We set ourselves a target of commissioning it by Q1 FY27, and I'm very pleased that we beat that and opened ahead of schedule.
We are not trying to just grow fast. We are trying to grow right.
This is an asset-heavy model by deliberate choice.
I don't want to take a guess of how inflation will play out.

up 9.9% YoY; OP and IP both grew

rows.why: Dombivli (500-bed superstructure, about 300 beds fitted out) is commissioned and Pune South is under construction for calendar 2028, with about 1,700 new beds targeted at about INR1.5 crores per bed; the BKC 400-bed hospital is approved but its opening date is not firm, so the surely call covers the commissioned and under-construction capacity.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Dombivli EBITDA burn of INR2-3 crores per month in FY27 with rising fixed costs, insurance tie-ups not expected until 6-12 months out, and rupee depreciation and capex cost inflation are the main risks to the plan.

rows.label: Dombivli insurance tie-up and NABH accreditation
rows.why: Management said insurance tie-ups are likely in 6-12 months and linked to NABH accreditation, which needs about six months of operating data from the February 2026 opening, and insurance is 55.4% of revenue.

rows.label: BKC land payment and 400-bed approval
rows.why: 25% of BKC land cost is paid and management said the remainder will be paid within this financial year, with MMRDA land allotted and clearances underway for the 400-bed hospital on over 1 lakh sq ft.
