rows.why: Gross debt is about INR500 crores against cash of about INR545 crores (net cash positive) at March 2026, and funding of the ~1,700-bed pipeline relies on internal accruals plus debt under a self-imposed 3x EBITDA ceiling, with detailed calculations still to come.

tone.note: Management was confident on Dombivli opening early and on budget and on the 3x EBITDA funding ceiling, but cautious on macro, declining to quantify base growth or inflation; analysts pushed on Dombivli ramp timing, the ~2,900-bed capex funding, and what drove ARPOB.

543980|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 total income INR411 crores, EBITDA INR79.3 crores at 19.3% margin, PAT INR37.5 crores; Dombivli drag INR9.5 crores.
543980|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter of operations for Dombivli Hospital, which contributed a INR9.5 crore EBITDA drag, in line with management's expectations. Consolidated total income was INR411 crores, EBITDA INR79.3 crores (19.3% margin) and PAT INR37.5 crores. ARPOB rose to INR73,500 and ALOS was 3.76 days, with average occupancy at 59.6% diluted by the expanded Dombivli bed base. Management kept Dombivli's guidance (EBITDA loss of INR2-3 crores per month on operating beds, breakeven in roughly 1.5-2 years) unchanged and confirmed the Indore expansion and a backward-integration IV fluids acquisition.

financial_highlights.value: approx. zero; roughly INR500 crores debt and INR500 crores cash (approximate, per management)

segments.name: Thane
segments.commentary: Occupancy stuck at mid-70s (about 75%); growth expected to track inflationary pricing with limited occupancy upside.

segments.name: Pune
segments.commentary: Occupancy in low-to-mid 60s; management expects growth to plateau or slow in percentage terms as the remaining ~15% occupancy headroom is filled, with pricing as a further driver.

segments.name: Indore
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 50%; revenue up about 10% YoY but EBITDA margin about 12% on new team buildup and doctor hires (a couple of crores of added cost). Expected to grow faster than Thane and Pune as occupancy improves.

segments.name: Dombivli
segments.commentary: First full quarter; occupancy roughly 25-30%; operating on about 200 beds with a further ~300 beds upcoming; fixed cost about INR6-7 crores per month; EBITDA loss guidance INR2-3 crores per month; oncology (radiation/LINAC) expected by year-end.

guidance_outlook: Dombivli EBITDA loss guidance of INR2-3 crores per month on currently operating beds retained; EBITDA breakeven guided at 1.5-2 years, with management saying the second year should be the breakeven year.
ARPOB expected to grow at inflation for mature units and above inflation for new units for a few years as case mix improves.

Ramp-up model: initial EBITDA drag for the first 1-2 years per hospital; after reaching about 60% occupancy on installed beds, capacity is added to bring occupancy back to about 40%, with some margin compression but no EBITDA loss.
Board-imposed debt ceiling of 3x EBITDA; current capex expected to be funded by internal accruals and cash, with debt possibly needed toward the end of the cycle.
Five-year visibility: all three announced projects to be delivered within five years; focus on Western India.
Management declined to give full-year FY27 margin guidance beyond the Dombivli inputs.
capex_capacity: Three upcoming projects on track; line of sight to around 3,000 beds with the growing footprint.
Dombivli operating on about 200 beds, with about 300 more beds to be commissioned.
Indore being readied for the next phase of expansion.
IV fluids manufacturing line acquired as backward integration for the pharmacy subsidiary, costing about INR35-40 crores including infrastructure; management says it is not a shift into pharma.
Management described the BKC hospital as a new site ~100 m from the bullet train station.
demand_pricing: ARPOB growth of about 10% in the quarter, driven by a combination of case-mix improvement and insurance contract renegotiations.
Dombivli payer mix mostly self-paid; insurance empanelment (cashless) still pending and expected to reduce friction and lift occupancy.
Dombivli oncology not fully launched; CGHS empanelment not planned immediately, to be considered later under revised pricing.
Doctor hiring at Dombivli to continue for a couple of years as subspecialties are added; ~30-40 full-time doctors plus visiting doctors at present.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Indore EBITDA margin fall to about 12% despite about 10% revenue growth, and is the 13-14% growth expectation for existing units realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher costs reflect new team buildup and doctor hires for the next expansion phase (a couple of crores). Management does not model unit-by-unit growth but said Thane will grow with inflation, Pune faster on occupancy, and Indore faster still.

qa_highlights.question: Is Dombivli's guidance still valid, and could breakeven come sooner?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance still holds (breakeven in 1.5-2 years); it is not being aggressive until one or two more quarters of data are in.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dombivli occupancy, fixed cost and doctor count?
qa_highlights.answer: Occupancy about 25-30%; fixed cost about INR6-7 crores per month, expected to rise somewhat over the next 1-2 years; about 30-40 full-time doctors plus visiting doctors.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company acquire an IV fluids manufacturing unit?
qa_highlights.answer: Backward integration for the pharmacy subsidiary to manage costs and improve margins; capital cost about INR35-40 crores including infrastructure, not a move into pharma.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Pune's growth slowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Pune is at mid-60s occupancy with about 15% headroom left; growth will plateau or slow in percentage terms, unlike earlier phases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and cash position and pledged-share issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pledge is by a non-promoter party, unchanged, with the increase in share count due to the split reported erroneously as a 5x pledge increase. Net debt is about zero, with roughly INR500 crores of debt and INR500 crores of cash (approximate).

risks_watch: Dombivli ramp-up: occupancy at 25-30% against an EBITDA loss of INR2-3 crores per month and fixed costs of INR6-7 crores per month; watch whether occupancy improves after insurance empanelment.
Thane and Pune occupancy plateauing near mid-70s and mid-60s, limiting volume growth to pricing.
Indore margin compression from expansion hiring ahead of occupancy gains (currently about 50%).
Rising fixed costs as Dombivli doctor hiring continues for 1-2 years.
Debt build-up for the capex cycle; management says internal accruals should suffice for several years.

segments.commentary: Acquired 70% stake in a curated platform of 73 hotels and about 1,000 rooms; under discussion for affiliation with Outdoor Collection by Marriott Bonvoy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 same-store revenue growth expected at 9-10%; total revenue growth underwritten at 10-11% with caution given the Middle East crisis, versus about 14% if no crisis.
Group EBITDA margin guided at about 38%, with 38%-plus maintained through the year; management says margins should reach 40%-plus on a normalised basis over time.
GST impact is permanent in absolute terms and has been about INR 7.5 crore YoY in Q3 and about INR 10 crore in Q4; normalises from Q3 FY27 on a YoY basis.
FY27 interest expense about INR 127 crore on existing debt; guided at INR 135-140 crore including a 15-20 bps rate-hardening assumption.
Net debt/EBITDA to stabilise at about 2.5x in 12-18 months; currently 3.07x.
FY27 capex INR 250-270 crore (about INR 150 crore for W Hyderabad, opening at end-FY27); FY28 similar run-rate, mainly Westin Bangalore. Total pipeline capex about INR 2,200 crore over five years.
capex_capacity: W Hyderabad (HITEC City) to open at end-FY27; expected to add about 6-7% revenue growth on a run-rate basis from FY28.
Pipeline openings: Tribute Bangalore Whitefield at end-FY28; Westin Bangalore Whitefield, Ingka Noida (162 rooms, variable lease) and Marriott Stiperumbudur (135 rooms, Chennai) in FY29-FY30.
Navi Mumbai 700-room Westin and Fairfield project announced; One Financial District Hyderabad (260 rooms) under development. Management excluded both from revenue and EBITDA forecasts.
GIC platform: INR 750 crore for a 35% stake in a 1,000-room upscale platform; INR 600 crore received, INR 150 crore balance over about two years linked to Westin Tribute Bangalore capex.
Over five years FY27-FY31, free cash of about INR 1,550 crore (flat base) plus about INR 1,000 crore from same-store growth; more than INR 3,000 crore cumulative after new openings, per management.
demand_pricing: QTD revenue growth (April-May 2026) is double-digit; April was flattish and May strong, against a weak May 2025 base affected by Operation Sindoor.

Q4 revenue growth ran about 12% through February before the Middle East conflict pulled March to below -1%; interrupted by the India-Pakistan conflict (May), August floods, December airline disruption and March Middle East conflict.
One-off disruptions cut FY26 revenue by INR 45-52 crore; management says underlying growth would have been 16-17%.
Management says inbound and long-haul travel is recovering (including US); repricing expected to restart as business rebalances. Occupancy described as strong.
Bangalore: about 17,000-18,000 rooms; supply growth about 5-5.5% CAGR, with more than half of future supply concentrated on the airport-Hebbal corridor where SAMHI has no presence.

Median flow-through about 55%, with 55%-plus expected; a Q4 margin drag came from a low-margin outdoor and corporate catering contract at Hyatt Regency Pune (about INR 13-14 crore), which management says ends from May 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How are April and May trending, and what is FY27 like-for-like growth after a favourable FY26 base?
qa_highlights.answer: QTD growth is double-digit: April flattish, May strong against a weak May 2025 base. Management expects YoY growth to stay in double digits through Q1 FY27 despite the Gulf crisis.

qa_highlights.question: Will GST be a permanent margin reduction, and what margins are expected in FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: GST impact is permanent in absolute terms, but management expects about 38% group margin, 38%-plus through the year, as pipeline is upscale with few rooms below INR 7,500.

qa_highlights.question: Is there construction delay risk, and will the focus shift to acquisitions or asset recycling?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating and growth teams are separate. Acquisitions stay opportunistic, guided by discount-to-replacement-cost, mid-teens ROCE and no long-lead greenfield. Asset recycling will continue with a few more candidates identified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue growth outlook including new openings, and the interest cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Same-store growth of 9-10% plus about 3-4% incremental from renovated assets; total about 14% if no crisis. Guided at 10-11% for caution. Interest guided at INR 135-140 crore including rate hardening.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins not improve in Q4 and what is the GST drag and lease accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites a low-margin catering contract (INR 13-14 crore revenue) that ends from May. GST drag is about INR 3 crore on a YoY basis per management's arithmetic. Variable lease payments (1.5-2% of revenue) go through P&L; lease-treatment impact on EBITDA margins is about 150-170 bps higher.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROCE target, net debt/EBITDA path and capex funding for FY31?
qa_highlights.answer: Current asset pool can deliver 14-15% ROCE. Net debt/EBITDA to stabilise around 2.5x in 12-18 months. Free cash base of about INR 310 crore assumed flat; management assumes no operating leverage and no EBITDA from Navi Mumbai or One Financial District; W Hyderabad and Ingka expected to add INR 400-500 crore EBITDA by FY31.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict: March revenue fell below -1% YoY and the effect is still continuing into April; management says it may keep affecting Q1 FY27 absolute numbers.
GST slab change (12% with input credit to 5% without) is permanent; margin dilution persists and sub-INR 7,500 room sales could rise in crisis periods.
Interest-rate hardening: management has assumed 15-20 bps rise; currency weakness is cited as a risk.
Bangalore supply: heavy Outer Ring Road and airport-Hebbal supply could pressure occupancy, which management says has already taken a hit over recent quarters.
Execution risk on pipeline (W Hyderabad end-FY27, Tribute and Westin Bangalore, Navi Mumbai greenfield) and capex of about INR 2,200 crore over five years.
Capital allocation: a Board-level discussion on buybacks or shareholder returns is ongoing with no commitment; asset recycling could extend to minority dilution at asset level (not committed).
Deferred tax income of about INR 330 crore is non-cash; reported PAT is inflated by one-offs and is not a run-rate measure.
key_quotes: So we do expect a 55%-plus flow-through. 50% is underwhelming, 60% is where we arc happy.
We're running really strong capacity utilization across the group.
Notwithstanding the share price or the discount Viraj, we are under a fiduciary obligation to create sharcholder value and allocate capital
But I think the discipline will decide what we do in future.
So I think structurally, the company will secure its place at 40%-plus reported margins.

543984|2026-06.headline: SAMHI Q1 FY27: same-store RevPAR up 9.6% to Rs 5,220 at 79.3% occupancy, while reported EBITDA fell 4% YoY on a one-time base and GST impact.
543984|2026-06.overview: Total income rose 7.3% YoY to Rs 308.3 crore reported, or 10.8% on a comparable basis after excluding Rs 9.3 crore one-time other income in the prior-year base. Same-store revenue grew about 9.1% and same-store RevPAR grew 9.6%, with occupancy up to 79.3% from 74.2%. Reported EBITDA fell about 4% YoY, which management attributes to a one-time Rs 9.2 crore GST impact and a prior-year one-time item; comparable EBITDA margin was about 12.1%. Management also sought a board enabling resolution for a Rs 750 crore capital raise, which drew heavy analyst questioning.

financial_highlights.change: +7.3% YoY reported; +10.8% comparable (ex Rs 9.3 crore one-time income in base)

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 100 crore (per analyst's math, not stated as a figure by management)
financial_highlights.change: down about 4% YoY reported; comparable margin about 12.1%

financial_highlights.value: about 3.2x TTM; about 2.4x for operating assets excluding growth capital

financial_highlights.change: about 300 bps lower than at IPO
unchanged since last upgrade in FY26

segments.name: Upper upscale portfolio
segments.commentary: Occupancy 78.4% in Q1 with RevPAR growth below mid-scale; management says the raw ARR growth was about 3.5%-4% across all segments.

segments.name: Mid-scale portfolio
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 13.7% with occupancy at 81.3%, outperforming the broader upscale portfolio in the quarter.

segments.name: RARE India (asset-light leisure)
segments.commentary: 75 hotels, 1,046 rooms across 15 states; management guides Rs 100-120 crore top line and Rs 35-40 crore EBITDA once stabilised in about 1.5-2 years, against about Rs 47 crore invested to date.

segments.name: F&B
segments.commentary: F&B revenue grew about 3.7-4% YoY against room revenue growth of about 14%, attributed to a shift to domestic guests, a Bangalore restaurant renovation and event cancellations moved into July-August.

guidance_outlook: Long-term same-store revenue growth expectation of 9%-11% reiterated; management says the same-store total revenue growth of about 9%-9.5% sits within this range.

Business plan targets revenue from about Rs 1,200 crore to about Rs 3,000 crore and cumulative free cash flow of over Rs 3,000 crore over FY27-FY31 (the call says Rs 2,000 crore once in error, corrected to Rs 3,000 crore).
Upscale share of revenue expected to rise from about 40%-41% today to about 60% by FY30.
Net debt/EBITDA of about 2.4x expected by FY28, not by end FY27 as an analyst assumed.
GST margin drag to be lower in H2 than H1; YoY GST impact of about Rs 9 crore to be removed from Q3 onward.
Early July trends described as ahead of Q1 exit, with growth split about evenly between rate and occupancy; management cautioned that one month is not representative.
capex_capacity: Seven new hotels in the committed pipeline total 1,660 rooms, mostly upper upscale and upscale; about 450 rooms are being rebranded from upper midscale to upscale.
W Hyderabad targeted for full operation in 2H FY28 (or calendar 2027); management flagged possible regulatory delays.
Courtyard Pune: back-office and MEP renovation under way; public area and guest room renovation deferred to about April 2027, taking 5-6 months.
Navi Mumbai (100% SAMHI-owned, outside the GIC JV): on-site start targeted for 1 April 2027, with a 3-4 year build; capex to stay small through FY28 and ramp in FY29-FY30.

Uttarakhand (Binsar, Almora) 8-acre estate Itmenaan acquisition for about Rs 12 crore; total leisure capital including RARE around Rs 60 crore, with management expecting leisure to stay near 10% of capital allocation.
demand_pricing: Office absorption in core markets about 11 million sq ft in Q1, against about 58 million sq ft for FY26; Bangalore, Hyderabad and Pune were over 65% of GCC leasing.
Passenger traffic was roughly flat YoY in Q1 after an early-quarter dip tied to geopolitics and Gulf carrier limits; the latter half recovered.
Domestic guests rose to 82% of room nights sold from 78% a year ago; 36% of days had occupancy above 90%.
Rate growth was soft because international guests, who pay a 10-20% premium, declined; management expects rate to recover in H2 as the mix rebalances.
Upscale and upper upscale hotels earn about 4x the revenue per key of midscale hotels on a same-store basis in FY26.
GST change from 12% with input tax credit to 5% without it cost about Rs 9.2 crore in Q1 and hits midscale rooms priced below Rs 7,500 more than upscale.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Khanna (Ambit): Why acquire the Itmenaan estate given weak revenue history, how is Leisure capital allocation growing, and what RARE opportunities are being evaluated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the hotel was idle for about a year and a half after owners moved to Canada and was delisted from RARE; it expects relisting and repricing toward Rs 20,000-40,000 rates in Kumaon. Total RARE capital is about Rs 47 crore, about Rs 60 crore with Itmenaan, and leisure should stay near 10% of capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Khanna: How much of FY27 growth is rate versus occupancy, and has July shown a sharp recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy drives growth in the first six months, with rate recovering in H2 as domestic mix rebalances from 82% toward a higher-premium international mix. July is 'trending far ahead' of Q1 exit, with rate growth now visible, but management declined to give numbers and cautioned one month is not representative.

qa_highlights.question: Jinesh Joshi (PL Capital): Are RARE sign-ups to the Marriott Outdoor Collection program on track, and why must the Rs 750 crore enabling resolution be taken now?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40 of 75 RARE hotels have agreed to join; management said sign-ups are ahead of its expectations and the pace is the issue, with 10-12 hotels on rival platforms. On the resolution, management said it will be taken every year so the Board can act in time; no specific deal is identified.

qa_highlights.question: Vikas Ahuja (Antique): Is the ADR slowdown (about 2.6-2.7% growth) due to West Asia disruption and Marriott-led inventory, and is occupancy at about 79% a tactical rate trade-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rate is soft because inbound international travel fell, and it focuses on same-store total revenue growth of about 9%-9.5%, within the 9%-11% long-term range. In July, total revenue growth split about half rate and half occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Vikas Ahuja: Why an equity-linked enabling resolution rather than debt, given the investment surplus discussed at the Analyst Day?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the resolution is a general enabling step to respond to unknown problems or opportunities and keep the balance sheet strong. It added that the Rs 1,200 crore to Rs 3,000 crore revenue path has no assumed acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Shrinjana Mittal (MS Capital): Is upper upscale underperforming midscale because of downtrading, and why is GST drag above 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw ARR growth was about 3.5%-4% across segments, and midscale RevPAR grew 13.7% at 81.3% occupancy versus 78.4% for upper upscale. GST drag is larger in Q1 and Q2 from volume sales below Rs 7,500, is lower in H2, and is about 2% per management.

qa_highlights.question: Vaibhav Muley (Haitong): Why did F&B growth slow to about 4%, and what is the GIC partnership scope?
qa_highlights.answer: F&B grew about 3.5%-4% against room revenue growth of 14%, due to a shift to domestic guests (80%-83%), a Bangalore restaurant renovation, and West Asia-related event cancellations moved to July-August. GIC has a right to 35% of new upscale deals post-JV, with no talks on existing assets; Navi Mumbai and W Hyderabad are 100% SAMHI-owned.

qa_highlights.question: Prashant Biyani (Elara): Timing for Grand Hyatt pre-positioning at Hyatt Regency Pune, W Hyderabad and Courtyard Pune openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Grand Hyatt repositioning is not being pursued. W Hyderabad is targeted for full operation in 2H FY28 or calendar 2027, with regulatory delays possible. Courtyard Pune public areas and guest room renovation is deferred to about April 2027 for 5-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Gupta (Asit C Mehta): How does RARE revenue recognition work, and what are RARE's revenue, margin and EBITDA targets?
qa_highlights.answer: RARE earns booking commission and, in some hotels, higher revenue share akin to franchise fees; hotel room revenue stays with owners. Management guides Rs 100-120 crore top line at about 35% margin and Rs 35-40 crore EBITDA once stabilised in about 1.5-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mahadevia (Moneygrow): Can RARE ROCE double the group's roughly 10%, and why is EBITDA flat while PBT is up 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RARE could reach 5x group ROCE and target 50%-55% ROCE, with about 95% EBITDA-to-PBT flow-through and no finance cost. On EBITDA, it cited the Rs 9 crore one-time other income in the prior-year base and about Rs 9 crore GST drag, with YoY relief from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Gianani (MC Research): Does the annual enabling resolution overhang equity, and how is ROCE on acquisitions in a costlier market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said such provisions are common among capital-intensive peers and no debt-equity mix has been decided. It said acquisitions still target operationally distressed assets, even at market peaks, with renovation, rebranding and asset management as the value levers.

qa_highlights.question: Ashish (Leo Capital): What is the Navi Mumbai status, timeline and capex phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legacy issues are resolved, with statutory approvals expected in the next few months and design work to be presented next quarter. On-site start is targeted for 1 April 2027, with a 3-4 year build, capex small through FY28, and main spend in FY29-FY30.

risks_watch: Rate softness from lower international inbound mix: rate growth is expected to recover only in H2 FY27, and July's split is one month of data.

EBITDA trajectory: Q1 reported EBITDA was down about 4% YoY; the one-time Rs 9 crore base item and about Rs 9.2 crore GST drag should fall out from Q2 and Q3, but management has not guided EBITDA figures.
Leverage path: management says about 2.4x net debt/EBITDA is reached by FY28, not end-FY27, and disputes an analyst's assumption of 2.5x by year-end.
Equity dilution overhang from the Rs 750 crore enabling resolution, which management says will be taken annually; no use or debt-equity mix defined.
Project execution: W Hyderabad could slip past 2H FY28 due to regulatory approvals; Courtyard Pune renovation timeline depends on April 2027 start; Navi Mumbai on-site start in April 2027.
RARE execution: Marriott Outdoor Collection sign-ups (about 40 of 75 hotels) and RARE's shift to fee income with limited disclosure of RARE RevPAR.
key_quotes: Same-store RevPAR grew 9.6% year-on-year to approximately Rs. 5,220, with portfolio occupancy at 79.3%, which was up from 74.2% in the year-ago quarter.
Put simply, every new upscale key we now add brings in more revenue per key and a better margin than the midscale it often replaces or sits alongside.
We didn't say 2.5x by end of FY 2027. We think we will get there by FY 2028, both because of EBITDA.
Navi Mumbai, we were originally planning to be on-site, hit the ground by end of this fiscal year.

543984|2026-09.headline: SAMHI Q2 FY27 same-store revenue grew 12.6% and consolidated EBITDA rose 12% to INR123.8 crores, with net debt cut to INR1,458 crores.

PAT was INR41.1 crores, but the YoY decline reflected a high base from one-time gains in Q2 FY26. Net debt fell INR35 crores QoQ to INR1,458 crores (3.1x TTM EBITDA; 2.2x after adjusting for growth capex). Management reiterated Q3 and Q4 as the strongest quarters, supported by a dense events calendar.

rows.why: Consolidated revenue grew 28% YoY to INR423 crore against a 40% FY27 guide, with DICE novation of about 85-plus clients completing by end Q2 and full pickup from Q3, so growth should accelerate from 18% stand-alone.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure was given, and capitalisation was cut to moderate new spend pending a policy review with auditors, so no new capex is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the 40% consolidated and 25% stand-alone targets despite Q1 at 28% and 18%, and gave no EBITDA guidance to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Stand-alone growth is 18% against a 25% target and program fees grew about 10%, so the 40% consolidated bridge depends on DICE revenue of only INR15-16 crore in FY27 and on program fee pickup.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Project Shiva (Zaggle Brain) is to be filed in coming months, the Zoyer rollout covers about 2,000 of roughly 19,000 stores, and co-brand launches with PNB and AU Small Finance Bank are underway.

rows.label: Program fee growth recovery and cash back discipline
rows.why: Program fees grew about 10% YoY (analyst calc), cash back is 66.3% of program fees vs about 69% in Q4 FY26, and management calls the slowdown 'by design' with improvement expected in coming months.

rows.label: DICE payments-rail integration and novation completion
rows.when: by Aug 31 / Sept 10 2026, full pickup Q3 FY27
rows.why: Majority of integration is done with the last part due by Aug 31 or Sept 10, and management called payments-related DICE revenue from Q3 certain, against an FY27 DICE target of INR15-16 crore.

rows.label: Limited MDR on high-value merchant UPI transactions
rows.when: depends on Taxation and Other Laws Amendment Bill 2026
rows.why: Management cited a possible limited MDR on high-value merchant transactions as a UPI monetisation tailwind, but it depends on the bill being passed.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term 14-15% margin aspiration, AI and DICE payments, but defensive and evasive on the growth slowdown, margin volatility and missing EBITDA guidance, repeating the 40% and 25% targets without new numbers; analysts pressed on the slowdown and margin volatility.

543988|2026-03.headline: Nuvama FY26 operating PAT crossed INR1,000 crore; Q4 operating PAT up 5% YoY to INR269 crore, with wealth and asset services driving growth.
543988|2026-03.overview: Management reported a growth year despite a volatile FY26 marked by tariffs, the West Asia crisis and subdued capital markets. Wealth and Private grew operating PBT by about 22-24%, and asset services recovered after a Q1 decline to end FY26 with revenue up about 12%. Capital markets (IB and IE) softened, with QIP volumes down and ECM subdued in Q4. Q4 firm revenue was about INR825 crore (+7% YoY; +13% excluding IE and IB), and firm ROE was 28%. Management says Wealth and Private now contribute 55% of firm revenue, and wealth, asset management and asset services together about 80%.

segments.name: Nuvama Wealth
segments.commentary: Revenue INR960 crore (+18%). MPIS assets about INR39,000 crore, with net new money about INR8,900 crore (about 30% of opening MPIS assets). Retention about 90 bps. Loan book about INR4,900 crore (+27%). NII about 20-22% of revenue.

segments.name: Nuvama Private
segments.commentary: ARR assets about INR54,000 crore; ARR yield 1.00% in Q4, with management guiding an average of 90-95 bps. Lending is 10-12% of revenue. RM headcount rose from 90 to about 150 over four years. Operating PBT +24%.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: Management fee income +31% YoY. Commercial real estate fund about INR3,800 crore raised by Q4, with the fund fully closed at about INR4,000 crore. Crossover 4 PE fund targets INR1,000-1,500 crore. Private credit first fund targets INR1,000-1,500 crore. Public markets roughly flat net flows.

segments.name: Asset Services
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR209 crore, above Q1 INR193 crore. FY26 revenue +12%, profit about +14-15%. Domestic RTA and trusteeship services expected live by mid-Q3 FY27. Global-local custodian tie-up on the verge of signing. Market share about 22% of chosen segments.

segments.name: Capital Markets (IB and IE)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR138 crore. Equity cash ADT -6%, futures ADT -14%, options +8% for FY26. IPO market share 19% by value and 15% by deals. Fixed income revenue +34-35% YoY, now about 50% of IB. IB/IE split about 30:70.

guidance_outlook: Asset services yields expected to hold at current levels; a possible rise over 12-15 months if inflation stays sticky and rates rise.
Wealth cost-to-income expected to fall about 100 bps a year over 3-4 years, with management choosing how much productivity gain to reinvest in RMs.
Private ARR yield expected to average 90-95 bps.
Management expects a good year in investment banking in FY27, with a 40-45 live mandate pipeline.
FY27 will carry incremental asset management costs for new strategies and the MF/SIF launch, which management calls investment rather than run-rate cost.
Bank guarantee norms expected to cost about INR10-15 crore a year net of deposit costs.
Private credit fund launch by end Q2 FY27; commercial real estate fund launch in H2 FY27 targeting INR3,000-3,500 crore (other remarks cite INR3,000-4,000 crore).
SIF launch expected after MF license, roughly two to three months from now.
capex_capacity: Commercial real estate fund: about INR3,800 crore raised by Q4; 40-50% deployed; three assets acquired (about 3.8 mn sq ft). New fund launch once about 70% deployed, expected H2 FY27.
Private equity Crossover 4 fund: about INR250-275 crore raised so far, target INR1,000-1,500 crore over the next 6-10 months.
Private credit: CIO Amit Kansal appointed; first fund targeting INR1,000-1,500 crore, launch by end Q2 FY27.
Virasat estate and legacy planning service launched; agentic AI tools deployed for RMs.
Asset services: RTA and trusteeship go-live expected by mid-Q3 FY27.
demand_pricing: Net flows in Wealth ran at 30% of opening MPIS assets; Private net flows about 22% of opening assets, in line with guidance.
Regret attrition: Private about 1-2%, Wealth about 3-4%. Management says AUM loss is limited.
Wealth RM productivity up about 25% YoY, helped by a lower share of under-one-year RMs (from 40-45% to about 33%) and AI tools. Private revenue per RM up 10-15% from agentic AI.
Private transactional revenue up 14% in FY26 vs ARR up 32%. Transactional revenue is about 90-95% broking and fixed income, with the rest deals.
Insurance volume growth moderated to about 25-30% from about 50%; management reports no yield impact. Category 2 mix may rise in volatile markets.
Industry view: new entrants offer high RM payouts, which management calls a caution; consolidation expected, with a few scale multiproduct leaders.
Mutual fund commission cut (April 1): management says impact negligible, as MF is under 20% of IE revenue and pass-through is similar to proposal.
Public markets: gross flows offset by redemptions, net flat for FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How should ECM revenue share be modelled for FY27 given large upcoming IPOs, and what is the impact of the MF commission cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites 40-45 live ECM and advisory mandates, and Q4 deal slippage is expected to recover. MF commission cut impact is hardly material, as MF is under 20% of IE revenue and net margins are similar.

qa_highlights.question: Is the asset services yield at risk as rates fall, and what drove the higher cash share?
qa_highlights.answer: Yields should hold, as rate cuts have already flowed through. The cash share rose after a large client was replaced by many smaller clients; the portfolio mix is about 70:30 to 75:25. A rate hike would lift yields as deposits reprice.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% wealth productivity gain from AI or from mix, and how do clients per RM evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it to RM seasoning (under-one-year share fell to about 33%) plus AI tools. Net new money is the outcome, not the cause of productivity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for transactional revenue in FY27 and the insurance commission trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Transactional revenue is mostly broking and fixed income, which are insulated from geopolitics. Insurance yields are steady, with some first-year commission support from category 2 products.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost-to-income ratios evolve in Wealth?
qa_highlights.answer: Wealth CTI fell 130-150 bps this year. Management guides about 100 bps a year over 3-4 years, with reinvestment in RM capacity as the lever.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 asset management flow expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: PE Crossover 4 targets INR1,000-1,500 crore; private credit first fund INR1,000-1,500 crore with about half this year; CRE fund INR3,000-4,000 crore with 30-40% this year. SIF flow numbers to be discussed next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the Ultra-HNI book sits above INR10 crore, and what is the mix of wealth clients by geography?
qa_highlights.answer: Families above INR10 crore are about one-third of the total and contribute 70-75% of AUM. Tier 2 and beyond is 35-40% of Nuvama Wealth. Private: top 8 cities about 80-85%.

risks_watch: Capital market revenue cyclicality: ECM and QIP volumes softened in H2 FY26, and Q4 deals slipped.
Asset services sensitivity to rates and collateral mix; rate direction could move yields either way.
Competitive intensity from new wealth entrants offering high RM payouts; RM attrition (regret attrition about 3-4% in Wealth).
Incremental asset management costs in FY27 for MF/SIF launch and new strategies.
Execution on SIF/MF license (final inspection done), private credit fund launch and RTA/trusteeship go-live by mid-Q3 FY27.
NII lag: loan book up 27% but NII growth lagged due to ECL provisioning; processing-fee acceleration expected in Q1 FY27.
Geopolitical volatility (West Asia) and the impact on ESOP-linked lending and client flows.

financial_highlights.change: +7% YoY; +13% YoY excluding IE and IB
FY26 ex-IE and IB revenue +17% YoY
Q4 up 9% YoY; FY25 revenue +41% with cost +24%
Q1 FY26 was INR193 crore; FY26 revenue +12%

financial_highlights.value: Up 22% (ARR now about 60% of Private revenue)

543988|2026-06.headline: Nuvama Q1 FY27 record quarter: revenue INR909 crores (+18% YoY) and operating PAT INR306 crores (+16% YoY), with client assets at INR5.36 lakh crores.
543988|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly profit above INR300 crores and revenue of INR909 crores, with ROE near 30%. Client assets crossed INR5 lakh crores, and MPIS plus ARR assets together crossed INR1 lakh crores. Asset services grew about 34% YoY, but management warned that growth will moderate, and part of the fixed income windfall (INR15-20 crores) may not repeat. Cost-to-income was about 55%, and management guided to a full-year opex growth of 15-16% plus an unspecified new office lease charge.

segments.name: Nuvama Wealth (MPIS)
segments.commentary: MPIS revenue up ~20% YoY; assets ~INR42,500-43,000 crores (+32% YoY); Tier 2+ now more than 35% of contribution. Wealth cost-to-income down 160 bps; advisory yield framed at 80-90 bps for ARR.

segments.name: Nuvama Private (ARR)
segments.commentary: ARR assets ~INR58,000 crores (+20-21%); ARR net flows ~INR1,000 crores in Q1 after weeding out low-yield legacy mandates. FY target remains 20-22% growth of opening assets. Private cost-to-income ~70%, guided lower for FY27 vs 66% last year.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: PRIME commercial real estate fund closed at INR4,000 crores (target INR3,000 crores), ~40% deployed. Second CRE fund targeted at INR4,000-5,000 crores by end Q3. Crossover 4 PE fund at INR300-350 crores raised vs INR700-1,000 crores target. Quarterly cost INR30-33 crores, peaking at INR35-36 crores; FY27 cumulative loss INR35-40 crores.

segments.name: Asset Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR260 crores, +34% YoY, with ~20% QoQ growth. Management cautioned against repeating this pace; FY revenue growth guided at 20-25%.

segments.name: Capital Markets (IE + IB)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR180 crores, flat YoY. Fixed income in IB was strong after the 7 June G-Sec tax change; ECM weak with Q1 IPO fundraise down ~60-65%. Full-year cost-to-income guided at 36-40% for this segment.

segments.name: Offshore (Dubai, Singapore)
segments.commentary: Dubai broke even; Singapore expected to break even by end of FY27. Offshore expected to contribute 5-7% of revenue this year.

guidance_outlook: Full-year opex growth 15-16%: about two-thirds inflation and business-linked, one-third new initiatives; new office lease charge (Ind AS 116) to be added on top, not yet finalised.
Full-year consolidated cost-to-income around 55%, with quarterly swings of about +/-1%.
Asset services FY revenue growth of 20-25%, with quarter-on-quarter moderation expected.
Private ARR flow target of 20-22% of opening assets for FY27; private cost-to-income FY27 below FY26 (~66%) and medium-term 60-62% wealth target retained over three years.
Indicative FY27 net flows: wealth and private INR10,000-12,000 crores each; AMC INR3,500-5,500 crores.
Private transactional income FY27 expected at INR350-360 crores vs ~INR300-305 crores in FY26; 20% of transactional income is opportunistic.
Asset management breakeven expected to start after FY27, with revenue inflection from Q4 as new products launch.
Lending cost of debt: blended 40-50 bps could be added to the current ~3.7-3.8% period-end lending margin.
Management expects equity mix in managed products to rise from 30-35% over the next two quarters.
capex_capacity: Net RM additions: ~11% (about 15 net) over last 12 months, 6-8 in Q1; target 15-16% a year if markets allow.
Physical offices in top 70-80 locations; presence in 65-70 cities directly and 400-450 pin codes via external wealth managers.
Second CRE fund (INR4,000-5,000 crores) targeted by end Q3 FY27; long-term REIT platform being considered within 24 months.
Private credit fund: team build-out 2-2.5 months; first fund launch around mid-to-end Q3.
RTA and trustee offering rollout expected in about one more quarter; targeted at PMS and AIF clients only.
Office lease renewal under evaluation; costs to be disclosed at quarterly results.
demand_pricing: Private segment RM competition has intensified; management says the company is still adding RMs.
Management says private yields will stay in an 80-90 bps range; can exceed 1% when a blockbuster AIF II/III product is in a quarter. Advisory impact expected to show next year.
Advisory book (ARR) is ~INR13,000 crores of ~INR58,500 crores total; advisory share growing.
Wealth retention fell from ~90 bps to 85 bps, attributed to insurance seasonality and total-yield accounting effects of market mark-to-market.
Venture debt fund fees were waived for three quarters and restarted in Q1, lifting AMC yields.
Public markets had redemptions in absolute return and long-short funds, as clients shift to SIF structures; SIF licence pending.
Q1 IPOs: 8 (vs 15 in Q4 and 14-15 a year ago); IPO fundraise down ~60-65% YoY and QoQ. Pipeline reported to be building.
Fixed income IB activity was strong because of the 7 June G-Sec tax exemption; some INR10-20 crores of income may not recur.
Management flagged STT, intraday financing and bank guarantee collateral rules on derivatives as a monitorable, but does not expect a significant impact.

financial_highlights.value: ~INR1,000 crores net (INR1,800 crores in the prior-year framing used on call)
financial_highlights.change: Soft on net basis due to mandate cleanup

qa_highlights.question: Private segment cost-to-income is about 70%; when will it trend toward the 60-62% wealth target, and what RM additions are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is not a fair base: Q1 FY26 was 69% and Q1 FY27 is 70% with profit up about 22%, as variable pay tracks revenue. FY26 was about 66% and FY27 should be lower. RM adds target 15-16% a year if markets allow; net adds were about 11% (15 RMs) in the last 12 months and 6 in Q1. The 60-62% medium-term target holds over three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wealth retention fall from about 90 bps to 85 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance seasonality (higher Q4 and Q1 income on a lower denominator) and total-yield accounting, where mark-to-market gains lower reported yield when brokerage does not rise in step.

qa_highlights.question: Will the AMC/venture debt yield uplift last?
qa_highlights.answer: Venture debt fees were waived for three quarters and resumed in Q1, which is the main driver. Management said it will sustain unless the fee is waived again.

qa_highlights.question: Asset services: will growth be yield-driven rather than flow-driven, and what is the FY cost-to-income for capital markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Flows continue, but some collateral may shift from cash to G-Secs, so yield adjusts. Capital markets full-year cost-to-income is guided at 36-40%, with ECM and part of IE under pressure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the lending margin outlook and cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Current period-end lending margin is about 3.7-3.8%. Blended cost of debt can add 40-50 bps from current levels, since hedging on the MLD book (about 25% of borrowings) makes the saving swing by quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How should the ESOP/ESAR cost and dilution be viewed over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Company is moving to stock appreciation rights (ESARs) subject to shareholder approval. Management cited 7.5% pool and about 3% dilution at 20% annual price growth. Cost is about INR300-400 crores over five years, noncash, and roughly INR150 crores net after tax benefits.

qa_highlights.question: Is the advisory shift likely to pull private ARR yields lower, and how big is the advisory book?
qa_highlights.answer: Advisory book is about INR13,000 crores of about INR58,500 crores ARR. Private yields should stay in an 80-90 bps range, and can exceed 1% in a quarter with a blockbuster AIF product. Management said advisory's yield impact should show next year.

risks_watch: Asset services growth moderation: management guided against repeating the ~20% QoQ pace, with FY revenue growth of 20-25%, and collateral shifting from cash to G-Secs could change yield.
Fixed income windfall: INR10-20 crores of IB fixed income income may not recur; capital markets revenue is flat at ~INR180 crores with ECM weak (Q1 IPO fundraise down ~60-65%).
Opex and new office lease: FY opex growth 15-16% plus an unquantified Ind AS 116 upfront lease charge; the cost will be disclosed with quarterly results.

Asset management losses: quarterly cost of INR30-33 crores peaking at INR35-36 crores; FY27 cumulative loss INR35-40 crores; crossover 4 PE fund at INR300-350 crores vs INR700-1,000 crores target; public markets redemptions as clients shift to SIF (licence pending).
Derivatives regulation (STT, intraday financing, bank guarantee collateral) flagged as monitorable; management does not expect a significant impact. Private RM competition has intensified.
key_quotes: Our quarterly revenues crossed INR900 crores, and our quarterly PAT crossed INR300 crores, an all -time high for us.
There will be some amount of moderation as new client acquisition has happened and a lot of collateral is right now sitting in cash, which will get converted between cash and G-Secs.
So this year, we will end up at a cumulative loss of around INR35 crores to INR40 crores.
Our target for the full year still remains at 20 -22% of the opening assets.

543989|2026-03.headline: Sai Silks Q4 FY26 revenue rose 5.1% to ₹419 crore; FY26 revenue up 13.1% to ₹1,654 crore and PAT ₹141 crore.

543990|2026-03.headline: FY26 presales of INR82.5bn and record PAT of about INR11bn-plus (exceptional RMZ gain); net debt near zero; FY27 launches guided above INR150bn.

543992|2026-03.headline: Yatra FY26 revenue less service cost rose 24.5% to INR 4,824 mn and adjusted EBITDA 37.5% to INR 917 mn, but Q4 EBITDA fell 46% on MICE disruption.

Q4 was weak: revenue from operations fell 14% YoY to INR 1,890 mn and EBITDA fell 46% to INR 126 mn, driven by West Asia conflict cancellations and deferrals of MICE and international group bookings into FY27. Management said Q1 FY27 run rates are about 20% above Q4 and expects H2 FY27 to be materially stronger, while reiterating a medium-term 20% RLSC and 30% adjusted EBITDA CAGR.

segments.commentary: FY26 gross bookings INR 16,578 mn, up 27%; room nights 1,936,000, up 16%; gross booking margin INR 1,534 mn, up 37%, with margin rising from 8.60% to 9.25%. Standalone hotel margin rose from 7.7% to nearly 9%, and standalone hotels grew about 32% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the air discount rising and what is the take-rate outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 FY27 tracking better than Q1 FY26, and is the 20% growth guidance still valid?

qa_highlights.question: Holding company (THCL) restructuring status?

543992|2026-06.headline: Yatra Q1 FY27 gross bookings rose 17% to INR21,007 million, but adjusted EBITDA fell 39% to INR151 million on MICE disruption and Kanoo build-out costs.

Adjusted EBITDA declined 39.4% to INR151 million (12.29% of gross margin) and PAT was INR3.4 million. Management attributed the margin squeeze to temporary MICE disruption, air margin pressure from delayed Middle East airline PLB deals, and pre-revenue people and platform costs for the Kanoo partnership. No FY27 guidance was issued; management said it expects to provide guidance next quarter.

543994|2026-09.headline: JSW Infra Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17% YoY to INR1,481 crore, but PAT fell 11% to INR328 crore on forex losses and Fujairah's nil contribution.

Port EBITDA was flat at INR594 crore, with margin compressing to 49.4% from 53.1%, as Fujairah contributed nothing and coal terminals diluted mix. Logistics EBITDA more than tripled to INR81 crore, with the rail rake fleet raised to 78 from 42. PBT fell to INR431 crore from INR463 crore on unrealised forex losses and higher depreciation, and PAT fell to INR328 crore from INR369 crore. Management held the FY27 consolidated EBITDA target of INR2,950-3,000 crore, while revising logistics EBITDA margin guidance up to 28% from 24%.

rows.why: Management held consolidated EBITDA and trimmed port EBITDA, with FY27 port guidance cut to about INR2,550-2,560 crore; logistics upside is offset by Fujairah and Paradip moisture-driven volume loss.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA target of INR2,950-3,000 crore depends on H2 port EBITDA and rake deliveries of 32 in H2, while Fujairah is nil and storage demand has fallen sharply.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Jatadhar cargo handling starts end-March or April 2027 with Cape-size in Q3 FY28, and Jaigarh LPG berth operations by March 2027, but these are port capacity starts rather than discrete product launches.

rows.label: Fujairah restart in early November 2026
rows.why: Eight tanks are under FOIS commissioning with final permission expected around 29 October, but storage demand has fallen sharply, so Fujairah volumes restart is uncertain versus ~INR250 crore FY26 EBITDA.

rows.label: Interest income on QIP proceeds
rows.why: About INR6,400 crore net QIP proceeds held in mutual funds and FDs generate other income that persists until drawn for capex, against cash of INR1,693 crore; this supports PBT offsetting higher depreciation (INR175 crore vs INR149 crore) and finance cost (INR108 crore vs INR99 crore).

rows.label: Keni environment clearance
rows.why: Keni is awaiting environment clearance, expected in about 3-4 months, which may delay that project; Oman bids are due mid-November 2026 with work from Q4 FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on the held INR2,950-3,000 crore consolidated EBITDA target and the rake ramp to 110, but cautious on Fujairah and deferred FY28 logistics margins to Q3 or Q4 results; analysts pushed on rake margin and revenue scaling, Fujairah restart and demand, and the other income jump.

543996|2026-03.headline: Updater Services FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR2,960 crores, but adjusted EBITDA margin was 5.9% after the Avon provisioning hit; no formal FY27 guidance given.
543996|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 3% YoY to INR750 crores and EBITDA was INR49 crores (6.6% margin), with PAT of INR27 crores. For FY26, IFM grew 10% to INR1,995 crores and BSS grew 1% to INR966 crores, while adjusted EBITDA was INR176 crores after absorbing the Avon receivables provision of about INR23 crores. Management said standalone UDS PAT fell on front-loaded IFM costs, provisions, lower interest income and a one-time wage-code charge, and framed FY27 as a clean year. Management declined formal FY27 guidance and said acquisition talks are still live but not assured.

financial_highlights.change: +3% YoY (vs INR726 crores in Q4 FY25)

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 adjusted EBITDA (after Avon one-time hit)

financial_highlights.value: INR966 crores, EBITDA margin 8.8% (adjusted INR85 crores EBITDA per Amitabh, ~9%)

segments.name: IFM
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,995 crores (+10% YoY), EBITDA margin 4.5%; Global Flight Handling EBITDA rose to 6% from 3%, Fusion margin ~6% to ~8%, Washroom Hygiene margin steady at 37-38%. Management says IFM growth is ahead of peers.

segments.name: BSS - Denave
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR590 crores (+11% YoY), EBITDA INR26 crores (~4.5% margin); Q4 revenue +15% and EBITDA +~70% with margin 5.5%+. Added 49 new logos; new and existing enterprise business grew 21%.

segments.name: BSS - Athena
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR116.8 crores vs INR136 crores in FY25; EBITDA INR23-24 crores vs INR35 crores, margin ~20-21%. BFSI concentration fell to 81% from 86%; 4 new logos added, no new customer losses in FY26.

segments.name: BSS - Matrix
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR128.6 crores; EBGC (background verification) revenue fell 11% on IT/ITES hiring softness, Audit & Assurance grew 5.8%. EBITDA INR14.9-15 crores, margin ~12%.

segments.name: Avon
segments.commentary: Avon took about INR23 crores of provisions (INR3 crores in Q2, balance in Q3) on logistics and freight brokerage receivables, fully provided; legal action underway. Core mail room and integrated support business grew 9%. Avon Transport has been shut.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance; management expects to grow ahead of the Indian industry (industry grew under 6% in FY26).
Management expects a clean FY27 start, with the one-time wage-code, front-loaded cost and provisioning items not repeating.
Visibility on FY27 revenue of 85-90% from existing contracts, per management.
Management said it hopes to indicate the FY27 year-end direction on the Q1 FY27 call.
Early April-May signs are encouraging, and several large IFM logos are signed or pending approval.
capex_capacity: All 23 Global Flight Handling airports are now operational and generating revenue.
Denave is scaling AI-led digital workforce pilots, which were run with 4 customers in FY26, and plans to scale them meaningfully in FY27.
Athena is in POC stages on agentic AI with 3-4 customers and won 2 Agentic AI contracts recently.
Management said it will invest in technology and AI, and talent, from its cash pool.
Shared services across finance, procurement and payroll are planned to drive cost optimisation.
demand_pricing: IFM: 30 new logos added in FY26 across industrial, technology and commercial sectors, with higher wallet share from existing clients.
Management cites demand tailwinds from the new labour codes (effective November 2025), GCC growth and outcome-linked contracts.
Matrix A&A won 12 large clients across FMCG, retail, quick commerce and manufacturing; one large customer reduced spend.
EBGC demand is soft due to IT and ITES hiring and some softness in BFSI hiring.
Athena: losses of 2 major customers and a downsizing by another in FY25 and earlier drove the revenue decline; diversifying into healthcare, retail and real estate.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~INR450 crore cash pile be deployed, including acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said acquisitions remain the primary use, alongside organic investment in technology and talent and shareholder rewards. The Board will decide the split, and some form of reward is expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there early recovery at Athena, and what is the steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Major customer losses have stopped; EBITDA margin has stabilised at about 19-20%. Key priorities are customer diversification and scaling agentic AI, which is at POC stage with 3-4 customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BSS revenue fall sharply and margins rise, and what drove IFM's PAT decline and the other opex drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Athena revenue fell about INR25 crores and Avon Transport (INR40 crores last year) was shut. Denave grew 11%, Global 30%, Avon Solutions 11%, and Matrix was flat. Standalone UDS PAT fell about INR19 crores: roughly INR12-13 crores from front-loaded costs and ECL/EPC provisions, INR4 crores from wage-code liabilities, and the rest from lower interest income, after a INR9 crore non-operating gain last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is returns on capital low despite revenue growth, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IFM growth is ahead of peers (IFM +10%, group +7%). It attributed the margin drop to one-time items that will not repeat and said interest income is a capital-allocation outcome that will rise with treasury management.

qa_highlights.question: Why no buyback given the net cash position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash is earmarked for organic growth, acquisitions and shareholder rewards, with the format (buyback or dividend) to be a Board decision and some reward expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY27 revenue is already visible, and what is the FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Visibility is 85-90% from existing contracts. Management declined formal guidance and expects to give an indication on the Q1 FY27 call.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the pending acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: The deal is still on; due diligence is almost closed, but other negotiating items remain and completion cannot be guaranteed. Management is cautiously hopeful.

risks_watch: Avon receivables recovery: about INR23 crores fully provided, with legal action underway; any recovery would be upside.
IFM margin: segment EBITDA margin was 4.4% in Q4 and 4.5% for FY26; front-loaded contract costs need to unwind as management expects.
Athena revenue continues to shrink, and the agentic AI POCs have not yet converted to scaled revenue.
EBGC/Matrix is exposed to IT, ITES and BFSI hiring softness.
Acquisition outcome is uncertain, and cash deployment (M&A vs buyback vs dividend) is undecided.
Management reported a decline in standalone PAT in FY26 and is expecting a clean FY27, which should be verified against Q1 FY27 results.

rows.why: About INR450 crores of cash; management expects some form of shareholder reward this year (buyback or dividend, Board to decide), while acquisition talks are live but completion not guaranteed.

rows.why: Management says several large IFM logos are signed or pending approval and early April-May signs are encouraging, though no order values were given.

rows.label: Avon receivables recovery
rows.why: About INR23 crores fully provided on logistics and freight brokerage receivables with legal action underway; any recovery would be upside, but timing is unclear.

tone.note: Management was confident on IFM growth, cash generation and FY27 visibility of 85-90%, but cautious on numbers, declining formal guidance and deferring to Q1 FY27; analysts pushed on the standalone PAT decline, low returns on capital, lack of buyback and the Athena and EBGC drags.

543996|2026-06.headline: Updater Services Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR764 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of INR42 crore (5.5% margin) and PAT of INR30.3 crore.
543996|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 9% YoY to INR764 crore, with IFM up 11% to INR525 crore and BSS up 7% to INR253 crore. Consolidated EBITDA was INR42 crore at a 5.5% margin, with IFM at 4.5% (about INR24 crore) and BSS at 7.5% (about INR19 crore). Management declared an interim dividend of INR1 per share, about INR7 crore of cash outflow, and said it remains a net cash company. Management gave no formal guidance and pointed to Q1 as the indicator.

financial_highlights.change: +9% YoY vs INR700 crore in Q1 FY26
IFM PAT INR20.7 crore vs INR19.9 crore a year ago

segments.name: IFM (Integrated Facility Management, incl. Global and Avon)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR525 crore, up 11% YoY, with 6 new significant logos added. EBITDA about INR24 crore at 4.5% margin, with management noting this is stable and it does not expect further decline. Global reported its highest-ever EBITDA margin of 9% (vs 5% last year), and all 23 airports are operational. Avon core mailroom revenue grew 10% YoY after the transport business was fully shut off.

segments.name: BSS: Denave (sales enablement)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR161 crore, up 18% YoY, with EBITDA INR7 crore at 4.3% margin. Margin pressure came from a mix shift toward low-margin field marketing and budget timing at one large customer.

segments.name: BSS: Athena (BFSI customer engagement)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR28 crore with EBITDA INR5 crore, an 18% margin. Won 2 new clients that started in July on 2-year tenures, and started its first agentic AI engagement in May-June.

segments.name: BSS: Matrix (Audit & Assurance and EBGC)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 2% YoY and was flat QoQ. EBITDA rose about 76%, and margin improved to 13.1% from 7.6% (EBITDA INR4.2 crore vs INR2.4 crore). EBGC revenue grew 9% YoY to INR12.5 crore with gross margin about 21%. Audit & Assurance revenue fell about 2% as large audits slipped from May into June and July.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance; management said Q1 numbers can serve as an indicator.
Management expects IFM and BSS each to grow low double digits, roughly 9-12%, so the 67:33 IFM:BSS mix should hold.
Matrix Audit & Assurance results are expected in H2 FY27 as deferred audits land.
EBGC volumes and margins are expected to be sustainable through this year.
Cash of upwards of INR300 crore to be deployed across inorganic growth, brownfield organic investment and shareholder returns.
capex_capacity: Global: all 23 airports operational and generating revenue; expanding into training and aviation support services, including security training and regulatory certification.
Athena: another agentic AI project has customer approval and is expected to go live in August 2026.
Matrix: a dedicated sales team was built for Audit & Assurance to target large multinational audits and food and automobile sectors.
Acquisition: a pending deal is on hold over valuation differences; management said it is also reviewing a wider pipeline.
Labour: recruitment teams in Eastern and Northeast India redeploy workers to labour-short states such as Gujarat, parts of Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and NCR.
demand_pricing: IFM demand: strong commercial real estate, GCC expansion and enterprise outsourcing; management sees clients favouring single strategic partners. Management says its GCC exposure is limited (low commercial, no residential).
BSS demand: clients are prioritising projects with faster ROI and sales productivity; spending is selective in some global markets.
EBGC: volumes are recovering after subdued banking and BPO hiring; the company describes margins as volume-driven with a flat cost base.
Contracts are largely pass-through, and labour shortages in several states did not visibly hit Q1 results.
Seasonality: Q1 is seasonally weak for catering; Q2 and Q3 are festive peaks for consumer-linked IFM and BSS work.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Matrix margin improvement sustainable, and has IFM margin moderation from headcount additions ended?
qa_highlights.answer: EBGC revenue went from INR11.4 crore (Q1 FY26) to INR11.7 crore (Q4 FY26) to INR12.5 crore (Q1 FY27), and gross margin from about 12% to 21%. Management says cost structure is flat, so volume drives margin, and it expects this to hold. IFM EBITDA was INR23.6 crore vs INR23.1 crore YoY, with some cost and contract front-loading.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash balance be used, and are buybacks planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is above INR300 crore across three buckets: inorganic growth, brownfield organic investment, and shareholder rewards. The INR1 interim dividend is the first step. There is no buyback proposal before the Board, though management did not rule one out.

qa_highlights.question: Will the IFM:BSS mix change over 2-3 years, and can agentic AI matter for Athena?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the 67:33 mix to hold, since both segments can grow 9-12%. Agentic AI is in use for outbound lead qualification and inbound repetitive queries. Management said it does not see wholesale replacement of human agents in BFSI near term.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BSS margin fall from 11.5% in Q4 to 7.5% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to a Q4 FY26 Avon restatement that added revenue to last year's Q4. Excluding it, Q4 BSS EBITDA was INR19.1 crore vs INR18.9 crore in Q1, so margins are similar.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the rise in other expenses and the tax-expense swing quarter on quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose because of restructuring costs and transport provisions taken in FY26. Tax fell on a manpower-linked tax benefit in a couple of group entities, and the mix is also a factor because Matrix gets no such benefit. Management said the full-year effective tax rate is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the SIS share purchases and the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no discussion with SIS beyond public knowledge; it reads the purchases as a treasury investment. The promoter family holds 59.1%. The acquisition is on hold over valuation.

risks_watch: Matrix EBGC margin (gross margin about 21%) rests on volume growth and flat cost base; hiring in banking and BPO is still subdued and management could not give a timeline for recovery.
Audit & Assurance timing: large audits slipped from May into June and July, and management expects these results only in H2 FY27; watch whether they land.
Labour shortages in Gujarat, parts of Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and NCR; management says contracts are pass-through but the shortage is real and customer cost pressure could follow.
Athena agentic AI: approval cycles run about 2-3 months, and management does not see wholesale replacement of BFSI agents near term; watch conversion of the August go-live into revenue.
Denave margin pressure from field marketing mix and one large customer's budget timing; the 4.3% margin is below the BSS segment average and management has not quantified recovery.
Pending acquisition is on hold over valuation; SIS share purchases continue with no stated intent, and a buyback is not proposed but not ruled out.
key_quotes: We normally don't give formal guidance. So I think we will continue with that.
At this margin level, we do believe that we will not decline any further.
Right now, there is no proposal to buy back shares on -- in front of the board, and there is not a discussion on it.
We are not reading too much into it. There is no deal on the table.

rows.why: Management expects IFM and BSS each to grow roughly 9-12% (midpoint about 10.5%), backed by Q1 revenue growth of 11% in IFM (INR525 crore) and 7% in BSS (INR253 crore), 6 new IFM logos and 2 new Athena clients starting July.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex and utilisation were not discussed, so there is no utilisation figure to support a capex call; cash above INR300 crore is earmarked for inorganic growth, brownfield investment and shareholder returns with no specific project named.

rows.why: No formal guidance was given and management pointed only to Q1 as the indicator; the 9-12% growth view is an expectation, not a raised target, and the Audit & Assurance deferral and Denave margin pressure cut against an upgrade.

rows.why: Matrix Audit & Assurance revenue fell about 2% as large audits slipped from May into June and July, and the recovery is only expected in H2 FY27; labour shortages in Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and NCR could pressure customer costs even though Q1 was not visibly hit.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Athena's second agentic AI project has customer approval and is expected to go live in August 2026, after the first engagement started in May-June; Global is also expanding into training and aviation support services with no date given.

rows.label: Athena new BFSI clients and agentic AI go-live
rows.why: 2 new Athena clients started in July on 2-year tenures and a second agentic AI project with customer approval goes live in August 2026, though approval cycles run 2-3 months and BFSI replacement of agents is not expected near term.

rows.label: Buyback or inorganic deal from cash above INR300 crore
rows.why: Cash above INR300 crore is earmarked for inorganic, brownfield and shareholder returns, with no buyback before the Board but not ruled out, and the pending acquisition is on hold over valuation.

rows.label: Matrix Audit & Assurance deferred audits landing
rows.why: Large audits slipped from May into June and July, and management expects these results in H2 FY27, which would recover the about 2% revenue decline in Audit & Assurance.

tone.note: Management was confident on IFM margin stability, Global's 9% EBITDA margin and the Matrix EBGC recovery, but cautious on guidance and evasive on the SIS share purchases and buyback; analysts pushed on margin moderation, the BSS margin drop from Q4, tax swings and cash deployment.

543996|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11% YoY to INR812 crore and EBITDA rose 37% to INR43 crore, with margin up to 5.3%.
543996|2026-09.overview: Updater Services delivered 11% revenue growth in Q2 FY27 with EBITDA up 37% and PAT up 62% to INR32 crore, driven by margin recovery in both IFM and BSS. IFM margin improved to 4.2% as large contracts moved past ramp-up and upfront employee costs normalised. BSS margin rose to 7.7% on 11% growth, with Denave's profit more than doubling, while Global (aviation) faced softer traffic and Athena and Matrix showed modest progress. Management declined formal guidance but suggested annualising H1 numbers, flagging headwinds in Denave and Global in H2.

financial_highlights.change: +11% YoY (vs INR729 crore in Q2 FY26)

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and equivalents (incl. MFs and FDs)
financial_highlights.change: As of September 2026; no long-term borrowings

segments.name: IFM
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR560 crore (+11% YoY); EBITDA about INR24 crore at 4.2% margin vs 3.8% in Q2 FY26. H1 revenue INR1,084 crore (+11%); 7 new significant logos in Q2, 13 in H1.

segments.name: BSS (Denave, Athena, Matrix, Avon, Global)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR267 crore (+11% YoY); EBITDA about INR21 crore (+62%), margin 7.7% vs 5.3%. H1 revenue INR520 crore (+9%), EBITDA about INR40 crore (+36.4%), margin about 7.6% vs 6.0%.

segments.name: Denave
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR175 crore (+17% YoY); EBITDA INR10 crore (+110%), margin 5.6% vs 3.2%; PAT INR8.5 crore (+160%). Demand Gen faces ongoing headwinds; field marketing grew steadily.

segments.name: Athena
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR29 crore; EBITDA INR5.5 crore at 19% margin; PAT INR3 crore (+25%). No client losses; two new BFSI clients signed in October.

segments.name: Matrix
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR32 crore (+2%); EBITDA INR4 crore (+31%), margin 12% vs 9.4%; PAT INR2 crore (+14%). EBGC revenue INR14 crore (+15%).

segments.name: Global (aviation / ground handling)
segments.commentary: Softer quarter due to airline capacity cuts and West Asia airspace disruption; no revenue figure given. Management is pushing Global School of Aviation as a less cyclical stream.

segments.name: Avon
segments.commentary: Mailroom and integrated support revenue grew 4% YoY in Q2; a fraud-related issue is partly resolved with some recovery possible.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance. Management suggested doubling H1 figures as an estimate for the full year (H1 EBITDA INR85 crore, PAT INR62 crore, margin 5.4%) and said these margins are sustainable, with headwinds foreseen in Denave and Global.
BSS expected to deliver good full-year results vs last year, though margin percentages may be impacted in H2.
Global expects activity to improve in H2 with festive and winter travel, with steadiness returning around Q4; update due at end of Q3.
Effective tax rate for FY27 expected to stay in a similar range to H1 on a full-year basis.
Labor code PF ceiling change (INR15,000 to INR25,000): full-year impact at worst INR1-2 crore after pass-through, versus INR5-6 crore with no pass-through.
Long term: management expects growth of 11-12% to accelerate; at current rate the business would roughly double in 5-6 years. IFM internal productivity could add 10-15 bps margin YoY.
capex_capacity: Capex plans and capacity utilisation were not discussed in the call.
Acquisition: a target pursued earlier was dropped after valuation talks failed; no active talks now, though another opportunity is under consideration. A deal may not happen this year.
Denave is closing two small step-down subsidiaries, Denave Europe and Denave Korea; management expects no material financial impact.
Headcount at 77,157 (IFM 60,152; BSS 17,005).
demand_pricing: India office absorption reached a record 66 million sq ft in the first 9 months of CY2026; GCC leasing about 28 million sq ft in the same period.
White-collar hiring growth moderated to about 2% YoY in September; BPO, ITES and GCC hiring grew about 4%; traditional IT subdued.
IFM: industrial and manufacturing customers together about one-third of IFM revenue; client retention about 95% over a multi-year window.
Global aviation: domestic passenger traffic declined YoY in July and August, with winter schedules cut by most airlines on high ATF prices and West Asia disruption.
Athena: BFSI concentration fell from 85% in FY25 to 80% in FY26; agentic AI deployments now live and billing for two clients.

qa_highlights.question: Expected full-year EBITDA margins for IFM and BSS, and impact of new labour laws?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance. H1 margin 5.4%, EBITDA INR85 crore and PAT INR62 crore; management suggested doubling these as an estimate. Labour code PF ceiling change could cost INR1-2 crore at worst after pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the planned acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Talks fell apart on valuation and the company did not conclude the deal. It is considering another opportunity; a deal may not happen this year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR23 crore Avon amount be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: A very small part has been recovered and some amount deposited in court by the accused. Legal and police processes continue. Management has line of sight to some recovery, which would flow back to the P&L, but gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: How will Global and Denave grow despite headwinds, and has Global improved in the festive season?
qa_highlights.answer: Global is growing the School of Aviation and seeking more airport business. Management expects steadiness by Q4 and will update after Q3. Denave is pursuing outcome-linked Demand Gen and field marketing.

qa_highlights.question: Effective tax rate for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the full-year effective tax rate to stay in a similar range, with no major swing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate low, and how long will it last?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax benefits from 80JJAA for employment creation. Management says the company relies on it less than peers and expects the incentive to continue while employment creation remains a government priority.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term view and growth drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth of 11-12% should accelerate; at current rates the business doubles in 5-6 years. IFM levers are new logos, wallet share, productivity (10-15 bps margin gain a year) and higher-value MEP and engineering services.

risks_watch: Denave Demand Gen headwinds and uncertainty; management flagged margin pressure in H2.
Global aviation: winter schedule cuts, high ATF prices and West Asia airspace disruption; update due at end of Q3.
Avon fraud recovery is uncertain and legal and police processes are ongoing; timing and amount not given.
Hiring slowdown in traditional IT and BFSI affects Matrix and BSS demand; white-collar hiring moderated to about 2% YoY.
Reliance on 80JJAA tax incentive, which management says will be reduced over time.
Leadership changes: new IFM COO (Rajeev Bhardwaj), Matrix CEO transition from 1 April 2027.
