544004|2026-03.headline: IRM Energy FY26 revenue rose 9% to INR 1,066.66 crore and EBITDA 17% to INR 112.25 crore; management guides FY27 volume above 250 MMSCM.
544004|2026-03.overview: FY26 volume reached 223.67 MMSCM (+9% YoY), with PAT of INR 56.89 crore (+21% YoY, standalone) and CNG stations crossing 150 (up from 111). Q4 PBT was about INR 17.7 crore against INR 22 crore in Q3, as management attributed INR 4.2 crore of one-time items (JV receivable provision INR 1.34 crore and bank charges INR 2.86 crore) to the decline and said both would be reversed or resolved in Q1 FY27. Gas sourcing was disrupted after the Gulf conflict, with Fatehgarh Sahib industrial supply cut to 55-65% of contracts before recovering to 80%. Management guided to gross margin and per-SCM EBITDA improvement of 10-15% and double-digit volume growth in FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Total debt incl. lease liability (end FY26)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 22 crore in Q3 FY26 per analyst
guided INR 5.3-5.5 per SCM next year

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: Largest contributor at 61% of FY26 operational revenue; station network reached 150 (from 111, +26% YoY) with 39 added in FY26 and 36 targeted in FY27. About 40% of CNG volume is sourced from APM/NWG gas, with HPHT gas for the balance; management says 4% of CNG was spot purchase in FY26.

segments.name: PNG Domestic
segments.commentary: Added 83,262 domestic connections in FY26; Diu and Gir Somnath has crossed 10,000 domestic PNG connections.

segments.name: PNG Commercial and Industrial
segments.commentary: Added 496 commercial and 223 industrial connections in FY26. Industrial volume is affected by the Fatehgarh Sahib NGT order and gas cuts; management expects industrial growth of 23-24% in FY27 if the order is implemented.

segments.name: GA-wise: Banaskantha (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: About 49% of FY26 revenue and 47% of volume, with about INR 420 crore invested; CNG-centric with higher margins.

segments.name: GA-wise: Fatehgarh Sahib (Punjab)
segments.commentary: About 36% of FY26 revenue (mainly industrial PNG) and 39% of volume, with about INR 200 crore invested.

segments.name: GA-wise: Namakkal and Trichy (Tamil Nadu)
segments.commentary: About INR 257 crore gross block invested to date; FY27 capex planned at INR 150-180 crore. Management expects around 90% CNG volume mix initially, moving toward 70:20 CNG to PNG over one to two years. 71 TNSTC PNG buses running with 50 more due in May 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth expected at 30%+ over FY26 in management's words, with volume crossing 250 MMSCM 'or maybe much more'; the CEO also said 'double-digit' growth, and the CFO said 14-15% was not out of line.
EBITDA per SCM to improve 10-15% in FY27 from current levels of more than INR 5 per SCM; CFO guided to INR 5.3-5.5 per SCM.
Gross margin and EBITDA margin expected to be maintained in the 25-26% gross margin range, subject to how the Gulf situation unfolds.
Peak debt for FY27 expected at INR 70-80 crore, against about INR 49 crore of term loans at end March 2026 and a INR 45 crore sanctioned term loan.
Namakkal and Trichy capex funded from IPO proceeds (about INR 194 crore available at end March 2026); other GAs funded from internal accruals plus the term loan.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 184.35 crore, including INR 81.33 crore in Q4 FY26 alone.
Cumulative investment to date: Banaskantha about INR 420 crore, Fatehgarh Sahib about INR 200 crore, Namakkal and Trichy INR 257 crore gross block.
FY27 target: 36 new CNG stations (39 added in FY26); Namakkal and Trichy capex of INR 150-180 crore.
Network of 6,695 inch-km pipeline as of FY26; about 35% of the cascade fleet is Type 3 cylinders. Trichy bus stand CNG station planned.
First LNG dispensing facility commissioned at Rasipuram (Namakkal and Trichy GA).
demand_pricing: Gas cost pressure from APM ceiling rising to USD 7/MMBTU (from USD 6.75) and higher NWG-linked prices; management says the increase was passed through to CNG, industrial and commercial customers from April.
HPHT gas price via IGX reduced from USD 9.72 to USD 8.92 per MMBTU, offsetting some cost pressure.
CNG sales for April 2026 were in line with budget after the price pass-through, per management.
Fatehgarh Sahib industrial supply cut to 80%, then 65% and 55% of contracted quantity during the Gulf disruption, now restored to 80%; demand destruction is occurring in industrial.

Namakkal and Trichy: CNG demand nearly doubled YoY after the OMC CNG model rollout; 92-95% of new three-wheeler sales are CNG; CNG share of passenger vehicle additions above 15% in that GA (vs over 40% in Banaskantha).
Management says EV penetration in its GAs is negligible; CNG auto and taxi demand continues to grow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 given the Gulf crisis and sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: gross margin of 25-26% has risen YoY; management expects margins to hold in that range, depending on how the situation unfolds.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profit fall from Q3 to Q4 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a INR 1.34 crore JV receivable provision (Ni Hon Cylinders) and a INR 2.86 crore bank charge, both expected to reverse in Q1 FY27. The analyst noted PBT of about INR 17.7 crore in Q4 vs INR 22 crore in Q3, still a gap after adding back these items.

qa_highlights.question: When will the NGT order for Fatehgarh Sahib be implemented?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not pushing for immediate enforcement given demand destruction and gas cuts; it will press PPCB and CPCB once supply stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 volume and EBITDA per SCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth expected above 30% (to above 250 MMSCM); EBITDA per SCM to rise 10-15% from current levels of more than INR 5.

qa_highlights.question: How much CNG is spot-sourced?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 4% of CNG volume was spot purchase in FY26; about 40% comes from APM/NWG gas, and the rest from long-term contracts and HPHT bids.

qa_highlights.question: What funds the Namakkal and Trichy capex?
qa_highlights.answer: IPO proceeds of about INR 194 crore at end March 2026; other GAs are funded through internal accruals and a term loan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the treasury income and cash flow treatment?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury income from liquid and overnight funds was about INR 68 lakh in Q4 FY26, per management, versus about INR 2 crore cited by the analyst as the quarter figure.

risks_watch: Gas sourcing: APM ceiling increase, NWG price rise and Gulf supply disruption could pressure margins if pass-through slows; management says CNG and domestic are insulated.
Fatehgarh Sahib industrial volumes: NGT-linked restrictions, demand destruction and gas cuts; implementation timing is uncertain.
Q1 FY27 must show reversal of the INR 1.34 crore JV provision and INR 2.86 crore bank charge, as management stated.
Execution of 36 CNG station additions and INR 150-180 crore Namakkal and Trichy capex; the new Tamil Nadu government's policy stance was flagged as a source of difficulty.
Employee cost rise (headcount from 214 to 256) and a INR 60 lakh labour code provision; license fee at 2% of net revenue.
Management declined to give firm numeric guidance, citing an evolving situation; several outlook figures were given as ranges and 'maybe' targets.
544004|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the FY26 operating record and the CNG and network expansion, but cautious on near-term guidance, which management described as hard to predict given the Gulf disruption. Management was defensive when questioned on the Q4 profit decline, attributing it to one-time items, and gave a hedged, range-based outlook.
key_quotes: So the gross margins that we see, they are in the range of 25% to 26%. They have increased from previous year.
We are expecting that in all four segments, we will be growing more than 20% year-on-year.
CNG remains the largest contributor to the volume, accounting for 61% of total operational revenue in FY'26.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided EBITDA per SCM up 10-15% from more than INR 5 (CFO: INR 5.3-5.5), and the APM ceiling rise to USD 7/MMBTU was passed through to customers from April, though gross margin is held to 25-26% subject to the Gulf situation.

rows.why: Network goes from 150 to about 186 stations with 36 targeted in FY27 after 39 added in FY26, and INR 150-180 crore Namakkal/Trichy capex is planned with IPO proceeds of about INR 194 crore available at end March 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volume guided above 250 MMSCM against 223.67 MMSCM in FY26 (about 12%+ on the stated floor, 30%+ per management), backed by 36 new CNG stations and Namakkal/Trichy CNG demand nearly doubling YoY, offset by industrial demand destruction.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY26 capex was INR 184.35 crore (INR 81.33 crore in Q4 alone) and management guided a further INR 150-180 crore for Namakkal and Trichy in FY27, so further capex disclosures are expected, though the brief does not give a utilisation figure.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided volume above 250 MMSCM (30%+ growth) but also said 'double-digit' and the CFO said 14-15%, so the range is wide and the upper end depends on how CNG demand holds in Namakkal and Trichy, where CNG demand nearly doubled YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gas supply was cut to 55-65% of contracts for industrial customers during the Gulf disruption (now 80%), and industrial volume growth of 23-24% in FY27 depends on the Fatehgarh Sahib NGT order being implemented.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First LNG dispensing facility was commissioned at Rasipuram and 50 more TNSTC PNG buses are due in May 2026, but no new product launch programme was discussed.

rows.label: Peak debt capped at INR 70-80 crore in FY27
rows.why: Total debt fell from INR 140 crore in FY25 to INR 72 crore at end FY26 with net cash of INR 170 crore, and management guided peak FY27 debt of INR 70-80 crore against about INR 49 crore of term loans at end March 2026.

rows.label: Reversal of Q4 one-time items in Q1 FY27
rows.why: Management said the INR 1.34 crore JV receivable provision and INR 2.86 crore bank charge would be reversed or resolved in Q1 FY27, which would lift the INR 17.7 crore Q4 PBT against INR 22 crore in Q3.

rows.label: Fatehgarh Sahib NGT order implementation
rows.why: Management is not pushing for immediate enforcement given demand destruction and gas cuts, and will press PPCB and CPCB once supply stabilises, so timing is uncertain and industrial growth of 23-24% depends on it.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY26 record, CNG network growth and Namakkal/Trichy demand, but cautious and range-based on FY27 guidance given the Gulf gas disruption and was defensive on the Q4 profit dip; analysts pressed on the Q4 PBT gap and treasury income.

544004|2026-06.headline: IRM Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR 326 crore, with EBITDA ex-other income up 139% YoY to INR 62 crore and PAT of INR 34 crore.
544004|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with volumes at an all-time high of 50.9 MMSCM (up 8% YoY). Margin expansion was attributed to sourcing (HPHT and long-term contracts priced below spot), price realisations, and cost control, with management stating there were no one-time items. Industrial PNG volumes were hit by a 9 March 2026 government notification that cut industrial gas allocation to around 80%. Management guided FY27 EBITDA of INR 7-8/SCM for the remaining three quarters and says the current margin level will likely moderate.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 capex about INR 67 crore

segments.name: Banaskantha (GA)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 48% of Q1 volume and about 46% of profitability; CNG is about 51% of vehicle sales here. Station additions limited to 10-15 in FY27 as the GA is nearing saturation.

segments.name: Fatehgarh Sahib (GA)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 38% of profitability. CNG penetration only 6%; volumes hit by the industrial gas cut linked to the NGT order. Plans for 2 new stations in FY27.

segments.name: Diu & Gir Somnath (GA)
segments.commentary: CNG is 60% of vehicle sales; contributed about 8-9% of profitability. Entire commercial segment converted to PNG, with commercial connections now on PNG. Plans for about 5 new stations in FY27.

segments.name: Namakkal & Trichy (GA)
segments.commentary: Q1 volume about 6 MMSCM, up 102% YoY from 2.84 MMSCM; contributed about 5% of profitability. FY27 volume guidance 25-30 MMSCM (vs 14.2 MMSCM in FY26); about 15-17 new stations planned; more than 80 TNSTC buses running, with a target of 200+ buses.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA expected at about INR 7-8/SCM for the next three quarters; management later indicated overall FY27 around INR 7/SCM and said the 19% EBITDA margin may not be sustained.
Revenue growth of about 25% in FY27 guided; management said a safe range is around 20% or more.
Volume growth of 10-12% in FY27, with total volume targeted at about 250 MMSCM by year-end (FY26: 224 MMSCM).
FY27 capex of about INR 250 crore in total (INR 150 crore for Namakkal and Trichy, INR 50 crore each for Banaskantha and Diu & Gir Somnath / Fatehgarh).
Long-term goal of 20-25% revenue CAGR over the next five years.
Management said same-level performance as Q1 will not be repeated every quarter; performance will be subdued going forward, though it expects QoQ and YoY improvement.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR 67 crore; cumulative capex about INR 1,090 crore.
FY27 capex plan about INR 250 crore; management said it will not exceed this, of which INR 150 crore is for Namakkal and Trichy.
CNG stations at 153 as of 30 June 2026 (up 37% YoY), with 564 dispensing points across four GAs.
Station model mix: franchisee (DODO), OMC and company-operated; the company is moving away from daughter booster and LNG-based models toward online stations.
Diu & Gir Somnath: tap-off from GSPL pipeline and hookup with IOC and GAIL in progress; currently drawing LNG from HPCL's Chhara terminal.
demand_pricing: Pricing: Realisations up about 15% YoY and QoQ per an analyst's calculation (not disputed by management); management said price hikes are linked to sourcing cost and it will not pass on further hikes now that Brent is cooling.

Sourcing mix in Q1 FY27: APM and NWG about 32-33% (APM 21%, NWG 11%), HPHT about 35%, long-term (Reliance, GAIL and others) about 32%, CBG blending 1%, spot about 1%. Q1 FY26 was APM 27%, long-term 27%, HPHT 38%.
HPHT gas at about USD 9/MMBtu versus spot of USD 14-20; industrial volumes benefit from GSPC and Shell long-term contracts running to 2030.
Industrial PNG volumes were hit by the 9 March 2026 notification (about 80% allocation); CNG and domestic/commercial PNG not affected.
Customer base: 86,590 domestic PNG (+13% YoY), 589 commercial (+36% YoY), 228 industrial (+5% YoY).
Management said it is a price taker; competitors and alternative fuel prices are high, supporting margins.

qa_highlights.question: Were there one-time items behind the sharp rise in EBITDA per SCM, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-time items; gains came from pricing, gas sourcing and opex optimisation. It guided FY27 EBITDA of INR 7-8/SCM for the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sourcing mix and how has it changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: APM+NWG about 32%, HPHT about 35%, long-term about 32%. Q1 FY26 was APM 27%, long-term 27%, HPHT 38%; Q4 FY26 APM about 26%.

qa_highlights.question: Namakkal and Trichy volumes and FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 volume about 6 MMSCM (up 102% YoY); FY27 target 25-30 MMSCM, towards the upper end, vs 14.2 MMSCM in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan for FY27 and station additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR 250 crore; stations to be added: 10-15 in Banaskantha, 15-17 in Namakkal and Trichy, about 5 in Diu & Gir Somnath, 2 in Fatehgarh Sahib.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the NGT order in Fatehgarh Sahib?
qa_highlights.answer: The NGT order (February 2026) has not been enforced by the Punjab pollution board; supply cuts began 9 March. Management expects ramp-up once enforced and says new industries must use natural gas to get consents.

qa_highlights.question: Is the promoter license fee a concern and how might it change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a 2% license fee disclosed in the IPO document, not profit to promoters, worth about INR 20-25 crore for the year and already included in PAT; it cannot promise the rate will stay unchanged.

risks_watch: Sustainability of EBITDA per SCM: management guided INR 7-8/SCM for the next three quarters and said the 19% EBITDA margin may not hold, versus Q1 at about INR 10/SCM.

Sourcing dependence: HPHT (about 35%) and long-term industrial contracts (GSPC, Shell to 2030) underpin margins; HPHT supply runs only to a stated date and spot exposure is about 1%, so future gas price moves could compress margins.

Industrial PNG volumes: the 9 March 2026 notification capped allocation at about 80%; Fatehgarh Sahib ramp-up depends on Punjab pollution board enforcement of the NGT order, which has not happened yet.

Namakkal and Trichy execution: FY27 volume target of 25-30 MMSCM (vs 14.2 MMSCM in FY26) depends on spot LPG/LNG supply from IOCL, BPCL, Kochi terminal until GAIL and tap-off lines arrive, which management says takes 9-18 months.

Promoter license fee: 2% of revenue paid to promoters, about INR 20-25 crore for the year; management could not promise the rate will remain unchanged, and minority shareholders have raised the question of a ceiling or absolute cap.
key_quotes: We can say that for industrial, we had two long -term contracts, one is the GSPC, the other is Shell.
Saket, it'll be highly optimistic to say that same performance, as scale up as in Q1, will be repeated every quarter. But it will be definitely subdued going forward, not up to this extent.
We hope and pray, but we can't guarantee 19% always.
As of now, I can't promise you whether this will continue at a reduced rate or same rate or maybe abolished altogether.

rows.why: Management guides 10-12% FY27 volume growth to about 250 MMSCM (FY26: 224 MMSCM), with Q1 at 50.9 MMSCM (+8% YoY) and CNG volume +22% YoY.

rows.why: Industrial allocation cut to about 80% since 9 March 2026; Fatehgarh contributes about 38% of profitability and CNG penetration is only 6%, so ramp-up depends on Punjab pollution board enforcement that has not occurred yet.

544004|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 volume hit record 61.23 MMSCM (+12% YoY) and standalone EBITDA rose 77% to INR 47 crore, but management declined to guide Q3 margins.
544004|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue net of excise rose 29% YoY to INR 334 crore, with PAT more than doubling to INR 26 crore and PAT margin at 7.7%. EBITDA moderated sequentially from INR 62 crore in Q1 to INR 47 crore in Q2 because of higher gas sourcing costs and currency movement. A September HPHT allocation change by MoPNG temporarily cut gas availability for about a fortnight at the start of Q3, and management expects Q3 to be impacted, while still targeting roughly 15% EBITDA margin for H2. The company remains net debt-free with INR 45 crore of debt against INR 253 crore of cash and mutual funds.

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: CNG volume grew 23% in H1 FY27 and now accounts for about 66% of total volume value. CNG stations rose 34% YoY to 156 and dispensing points 36% to 576.

segments.name: Commercial PNG
segments.commentary: Commercial PNG volume grew 61% in H1 FY27; commercial connections rose 48% YoY.

segments.name: Industrial PNG
segments.commentary: Industrial volumes remained weak on relative fuel economics versus alternate fuels, with sequential recovery in Q2. Industrial connections rose 8% YoY.

segments.name: Domestic PNG
segments.commentary: Domestic PNG connections rose 14% YoY. Networks: MDPE pipeline up 20% to 7,313 km; steel pipeline up 17% to 3,441 inch-km.

segments.name: Geographic mix (H1 FY27 volume)
segments.commentary: Banaskantha about 47%, Fatehgarh Sahib 33%, Namakkal and Trichy 11% (up from about 6% in FY26), Diu and Gir Somnath 9%.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 EBITDA margin expected at around 15%, per management in Q&A.
Q3 FY27 expected to be impacted by the temporary gas supply disruption and higher sourcing costs; Q4 expected to recover. Management declined to give rupee-per-SCM or margin guidance for Q3.
Capex for FY27 guided at INR 250-260 crore; INR 111 crore spent in H1 (INR 54 crore in Q1, INR 57 crore in Q2), with bills in line and possible overrun.
Volume growth: management said it may revise the earlier ~12% FY27 volume plan by 50-100 bps to protect margins; no expectation of exceeding prior guidance, with some moderation possible.
Sourcing tied up through 2030 via Shell India, GSPC, IOC and GAIL; management plans further long-term contracts once geopolitical volatility eases, in about six months.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex plan of INR 250-260 crore; INR 111 crore spent in H1 FY27 with bills pending.
CNG network at 156 stations and 576 dispensing points; MDPE network 7,313 km; steel pipeline 3,441 inch-km.

IPO proceeds: INR 496 crore received; INR 358.68 crore utilised by 30 Sep 2026 (INR 170.18 crore CGD network in NT area, INR 135 crore debt repayment, INR 53.50 crore general corporate purposes); about INR 137.08 crore remains for Namakkal and Tiruchirappalli network.

Namakkal and Trichy: TNSTC MoU; 83 buses converted, taking CNG fleet to 183 buses in Namakkal and 55 in Tiruchirappalli. Connectivity work started under IOC (NT) and GTN (Diu & Gir Somnath) hookup arrangements.
Two GAs (Diu & Gir Somnath, Namakkal) still in formative stage; LCNG stations and compression services provided to BPCL at Namakkal and Trichy.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 volume an all-time high of 61.23 MMSCM, +12% YoY; H1 FY27 volume 120.16 MMSCM, +10% YoY.

Gas sourcing mix in Q2 (portfolio basis): APM about 21%, new well gas about 13%, HPHT about 33%, LNG about 30%, spot 1-2% (management cited about 0.5% spot in prepared remarks). Average cost about USD 9.5/MMBtu.
Per-source cost: APM capped at USD 7/MMBtu; new well gas about USD 10.2; HPHT about USD 8.9; RLNG USD 11-12/MMBtu.
Spot gas volatile: management cited spikes to USD 29-32/MMBtu and drops to USD 19-24/MMBtu. Spot purchases to cover shortfalls raised sourcing cost.

Raw material cost rose about INR 1.2 per SCM QoQ, attributed to HPHT allocation changes, Brent-linked pricing and dollar rate movement. Price hikes passed through to consumers, with CNG kept below petrol price.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a rethink on royalty paid to promoters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is comfortable with the current arrangement; royalty (2% of revenue from operations, booked in other expenses) continues until settlement, as per the IPO prospectus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sourcing mix and cost per MMBtu by source?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 mix: APM about 21%, NWG about 13%, HPHT about 33%, LNG about 30%, spot 1-2%. Average about USD 9.5/MMBtu; APM capped at USD 7, NWG about USD 10.2, HPHT about USD 8.9, RLNG USD 11-12.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q3 raw material cost rise and what is the HPHT impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The 3 September MoPNG HPHT methodology change favoured large players and hurt smaller ones. About 80% of the correction is done after the 19 October relaxation; the transition impact lasted about 20 days to one month. Brent and dollar movements added to costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why will Q3 not be as strong sequentially?

544009|2026-03.headline: Blue Jet FY26 revenue fell 8% to INR947 crores on PI/API destocking, while Q4 contrast media revenue rose 91% YoY to INR193 crores.
544009|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was INR947 crores, down 8% YoY, with reported EBITDA margin at 31% versus 37% in FY25 as PI/API volumes fell 35%. Contrast media was the offset, growing 23% to INR495 crores for the year and 91% YoY in Q4 to INR193 crores. Management said PI/API destocking is complete and shipments are resuming, and it is ramping investment in Vizag (about INR1,000 crores over roughly 3 years), Mahad Unit 3 and a Hyderabad R&D centre. The company remains debt-free with INR400 crores of liquid assets.

segments.name: Contrast media
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR495 crores (+23%); Q4 INR193 crores (+91% YoY). Flagship product volumes up vs FY25 despite goods in transit; customer FY27 forecast implies mid-single-digit growth for that product. NCE intermediate commercialised in FY25 saw strong FY26 offtake.

segments.name: PI/API (pharma intermediates)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR298 crores (-35%), driven by destocking of a cardiovascular intermediate by an innovator customer. Q4 revenue collapsed to INR2.4 crores from INR40 crores in Q3, with management saying destocking is now complete.

segments.name: Artificial sweetener
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR131 crores (-2%); Q4 INR37 crores (+43% QoQ, -24% YoY). Management cited pricing pressure from imports; one high-volume product is under validation with trial shipments expected over coming quarters.

guidance_outlook: Contrast media: management expects double-digit growth in FY27, backed by one or two validations and one commercial launch; molecules include gadolinium and iodinated products. Management declined to quantify.
PI/API: management expects FY27 to exceed the FY25 peak, citing supply-network participation with the innovator customer, but gave no formal guidance.
Margins: management would not guide FY27 margins; Q1 FY27 cost structure to be assessed. Freight costs rose after March 2026 and the FY27 logistics impact is still to be evaluated.
Mahad Unit 3 (backward integration) expected to start production in H2 FY27, with a slow ramp-up.
Hyderabad R&D centre (about INR40 crores) to go live in H2 FY27; product development spend to rise in FY27.
FY27 capex of roughly INR400 crores across Vizag, completion of Mahad and Ambernath additions.
Vizag capacity expected online in 24-30 months; 3-4 contrast media launches and about 2 PI/CDMO opportunities expected to reach commercialisation in FY27.
capex_capacity: Vizag greenfield (about 100 acres): total capex about INR1,000 crores over about 3 years; Phase 1 covers contrast media intermediates, high-intensity sweeteners and pharma intermediates; development activities underway after groundbreaking.
Mahad Unit 3: backward integration project for a key contrast media raw material is progressing; plant expected to go onstream this year.
Mahad facility in final stages of completion; commercial production expected H2 FY27.
Management says contrast media is far from peak utilisation due to ongoing debottlenecking and capacity creation.
Hyderabad R&D centre (about INR40 crores) for peptide intermediates, GLP-1-linked chemistry, biocatalysts and faster CDMO development turnaround.
demand_pricing: PI/API: destocking has happened and the plant is running at optimum capacity; management said the worst is behind for this segment.

Pipeline: about 20 active RFPs in PI/CDMO, mainly chronic therapy areas including GLP-1 and peptide building blocks; 2 expected to commercialise this year. Two high-conviction lateral entries are being evaluated, with dedicated Vizag capacity planned.
Peptides: lab supplies started to some innovators and large peptide CDMOs; management flagged faster price erosion risk in peptides than in contrast media or patented CDMO work.
Artificial sweetener: pricing pressure from imports; management will remain opportunistic.
Raw material costs rose in the last month of FY26 due to the Iran war; rupee depreciation offset this in FY26 and the company is in pass-through discussions with select customers.
Warning letter at one customer's sole formulation plant: management said there is no import alert and no current supply disruption.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence PI will exceed the FY25 peak, and is it confirmed?
qa_highlights.answer: VK Singh said destocking is done, some orders were held back and deferred, and new orders have come in after supply-chain realignment. New products will take time, so little is factored in.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 contrast media revenue is from goods shipped in Q3 (INR190 crores vs INR125 crores in Q3)?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Karuppannan said goods in transit have normalised with no significant variance, so the full INR190 crores belongs to Q4 order book.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 a step-jump year for contrast media?
qa_highlights.answer: Shiven Arora said the focus is double-digit growth backed by new launches, and declined to say more about a step-jump.

qa_highlights.question: Will Mahad backward integration drive margins or top line?
qa_highlights.answer: VK Singh said the primary aim was supply independence from import price volatility; the two products also open third-party sales, but no numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 given freight and crude pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Karuppannan said it is too early to comment and that Q1 FY27 cost structures would be the better guide.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company raising funds, and is it linked to Vizag?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Karuppannan said the situation is dynamic and an update will follow in coming quarters; the company is accelerating capex from its debt-free balance sheet.

risks_watch: FY27 margin pressure from freight and crude-linked raw material costs; management has not quantified the impact.
Contrast media growth depends on FY27 validations and launches, and monthly offtake is uneven; the FY26 Q4 surge may not be repeatable.
Vizag execution: about INR1,000 crores over 3 years, with a 24-30 month window for online capacity; FY27 capex about INR400 crores.
Customer regulatory risk: a warning letter at a customer's plant (no import alert yet) and a patent-protected molecule under change of ownership.
Peptide price erosion risk, and artificial sweetener import-driven pricing pressure.
Possible fundraise, with no detail given on size or use.
544009|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on contrast media and on PI recovery, but guarded on margins and specifics; management withheld customer, molecule and pricing detail under confidentiality and declined to guide margins until Q1 FY27.

So we are quite confident that in the PI segment, we are getting to a very good set of numbers in the coming year.
So from our standpoint, business as usual.

544009|2026-06.headline: Blue Jet Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25% QoQ to INR293 crore and EBITDA hit INR98 crore, with PI/API restart offset by INR30 crore contrast media goods in transit.
544009|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR293 crore, up 25% QoQ, with operating EBITDA margin of 33.5% versus 30.4% in Q4 FY26. Growth came mainly from PI and API, where supply of an intermediate restarted after customer destocking. Contrast media revenue fell sharply (about 40% QoQ per analyst) because roughly INR30 crore of goods were in transit at quarter end, which management says will be recognised next quarter. Raw material inflation from March 2026 weighed on gross margin, which fell about 3 points to 53%. Mahad (Unit 3) is now expected to commission later this calendar year, slightly ahead of the earlier H2 guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR2-3 crore earlier; mainly export incentive and forex gain per management

financial_highlights.value: ~INR30 crore higher at closing vs opening
financial_highlights.change: to be recognised in Q2 FY27

segments.name: PI / API (Bempedoic-acid related intermediate)
segments.commentary: Main driver of QoQ growth after restarting supply hit by customer destocking. Management cites a strong order book and visibility for at least the next 3-4 quarters.

segments.name: Contrast media
segments.commentary: Revenue declined QoQ because about INR30 crore of goods were in transit at quarter end; plant at ~70% utilisation. Management describes the segment as stable with long-term arrangements.

segments.name: High-intensity sweetener
segments.commentary: Stable contributor per management; new sweetener is in pilot validation at the existing facility, with scale-up planned at Vizag.

segments.name: Iodinated contrast media intermediate (ABA-HCL)
segments.commentary: Commercial batches expected to start shortly; positive trend seen by end Q2 or beginning Q3 FY27.

Backward integration project at Unit 3 on track for commercial contribution in H2 FY27.

Raw material price trend uncertain; price pass-through to customers expected with a few quarters' lag, evaluated case by case.

Hyderabad R&D centre: first phase expected to be operational in August 2026; scientific talent already onboarded.

Peptides: focus on peptide fragments (liquid phase) rather than generic front-end peptides, where management sees price erosion.

qa_highlights.question: Contrast media revenue fell ~40% QoQ; how much revenue is deferred to Q2 and what is utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing goods in transit were about INR30 crore higher than opening, which will be recognised next quarter. Plant utilisation is ~70% steady; production unchanged and production-to-dispatch at 100%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating income jump to INR16.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the bulk to forex gain and higher interest income, and later clarified the line item is driven mainly by export incentives tied to export levels and byproduct sales; the ratio to exports should remain in a similar range.

qa_highlights.question: Is PI/API growth lumpy or secular, and what visibility exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: secular growth in end-market demand plus a strong order book and consistent production give good visibility for at least 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Vizag and cardiovascular-related opportunity translate into sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to speculate, saying it will go by orders on hand; order book described as good and an update to come when more information is available.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the peptides strategy and differentiation from other Indian CDMOs?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on peptide fragments first (liquid phase), with selective forward integration into final peptides for large CDMOs or innovators; no participation in generic front-end peptides. Management intends to quantify the peptide-related RFPs in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Do you maintain FY27 capex guidance and what is the asset turn outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR250 crore; company-level FY27 capex of INR400 crore similar. Asset turn to be assessed on commercialisation from end FY29-FY30, with ramp-up around FY31-FY32.

544009|2026-09.headline: Blue Jet Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR376 crore (up 28% QoQ), but gross margin fell to 49% on West Asia-driven raw material costs.
544009|2026-09.overview: Blue Jet reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue from operations of about INR376 crore in Q2 FY27, with EBITDA of about INR119 crore and PAT of about INR103 crore, marking the fourth straight quarter of sequential growth. Growth came from contrast media (+25% QoQ) and PI API (+52% QoQ), while artificial sweetener fell 30% QoQ. Gross margin slipped to 49% (down 4 points QoQ) as higher reagent, solvent and catalyst costs from the West Asia disruption were only partly passed on, with some customer price increases effective from Q3. Management declined to guide on sustainability of run-rate revenue, and it reiterated Mahad Unit 3 start-up in H2 FY27 and phased Vizag capex.

544012|2026-03.headline: Cello World Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR654 crore (record quarter), but EBITDA margin fell to 20.9%; FY27 revenue guided at 10-12% growth.
544012|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was a record INR653.6 crore, up 11% YoY, with EBITDA of INR136.6 crore (20.9% margin) and PAT of INR90.1 crore (13.8% margin). FY26 revenue grew 8.8% to INR2,323.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR526.4 crore (22.7%) and PAT margin of 14.3%, weighed down by glassware losses and steel bottle ramp-up costs. Management described FY26 as a year of corrective initiatives and said Q1 FY27 looks challenging due to the Middle East-linked cost and demand headwinds. Steel bottle capacity is ramping in phases toward full scale by July 2026, and the Wimplast merger and a restructuring scheme took effect from 27 May 2026.

Management declined to guide for FY27 and said it would be better placed to do so next quarter.

ST LAP origination yield has fallen from 16.1% to 14.9% over 5-6 quarters; management attributed this to state mix and competition, not ticket size, and said yields should improve in Q3.

544028|2026-09.headline: Tata Technologies Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.2% YoY in constant currency to US$178M; operating EBITDA margin held at 16.1% despite salary increments.

Total revenue in INR rose 2.1% QoQ to INR 1,699 crore, held back by a Technology Solutions decline tied to a revenue-recognition change and education timing. Operating EBITDA margin was 16.1%, flat QoQ, absorbing a ~100bp salary-increment headwind, and PAT was INR 171 crore. Management reiterated strong double-digit FY27 growth and said margins should expand in H2, while ES-Tec (Germany) remains soft.

544029|2026-03.headline: Gandhar Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to INR1,093 crore, with FY26 PAT at INR137 crore and EBITDA margin about 5.5-6%.
544029|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR1,093 crore (up 14% YoY) and Q4 EBITDA was INR64 crore, up both QoQ and YoY, with PAT of INR37 crore versus INR12 crore a year earlier. FY26 revenue reached INR4,241 crore (about 9-10% growth), EBITDA INR234 crore and PAT INR137 crore. Operating cash flow improved to INR127.77 crore from INR14.71 crore. Management said Middle East disruption (Strait of Hormuz) caused base oil price volatility and freight pressure, but pass-through pricing and sourcing changes mitigated the impact. Plants ran above nameplate capacity on a multi-shift basis, and Taloja land and a South Africa subsidiary were flagged as future growth steps without firm capex numbers.

segments.name: PHPO (personal care, healthcare, performance oil)
segments.commentary: About 50% of revenue; management calls it the company's core focus, with a stated growth rate of about 4% CAGR over the next 4-5 years (as stated on the call).

segments.name: Lubricants
segments.commentary: About 27% of revenue in FY26.

segments.commentary: About 10.19% of revenue in FY26. Transformer oil is also part of the mix, but no separate margin or price trend was disclosed.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Exports were about 42.8% of consolidated revenue in the prepared remarks, and about 45% in Q&A (range given as 45-48%). Sales go to 100+ countries. US exposure is described as minimal.

guidance_outlook: Management expects consolidated EBITDA margin of about 6% to be maintained in coming quarters, but gave no hard numeric target.
Management is working on a two-year capacity expansion plan; capex budget clarity is expected in the next 2-3 quarters.
Debt-to-equity is practically nil standalone; management expects to maintain it except for any borrowing for the South Africa expansion.
Management said it is open to inorganic growth opportunities.
Volume growth of close to double digits has been historical; management expects revenue growth to continue, but declined to give formal multi-year guidance.
capex_capacity: India plants (Taloja and Silvassa) installed capacity is 3,62,100 kL on a 2-shift basis; output was 4,58,853 kL, about 125-126% utilisation, using 3-shift operation in some months.
Group installed capacity is 5,97,403 kL including Sharjah (Texol, Hamriyah Free Zone). Output of 5,54,212 kL gives about 93% utilisation.
Sharjah (Texol) is underutilised due to port and shipping disruption; management expects utilisation to ramp up once the situation normalises.

A plot of land was bought at Taloja for plant expansion. Management said the Taloja facility is close to 100% utilised. Panvel land acquisition was referenced by an analyst but not discussed by management.

Board has given broad approval for a South Africa investment (analyst cited INR50 crore); the company has only just set up a South African entity and has not decided between office and plant. No investment is planned yet, per management.
demand_pricing: Management described the global white oil market as about USD1.93 billion in 2026, rising to about USD2.75 billion by 2033 (about 5.5% CAGR), led by Asia Pacific.
Base oil prices rose about 20-25% in the past month versus about 10% for crude, per management. Pricing is mostly index-linked or spot, with fortnightly price revisions to customers.
Pass-through contracts cover about 35-40% of customers; the rest are repriced through fortnightly revisions.

Raw material sourcing: about 20-22% comes from Middle East suppliers. Sourcing has shifted toward Korean suppliers and domestic refiners (BPCL, IOCL). Suppliers including Aramco and ADNOC are reportedly supplying via alternate routes.
Freight: most export sales are FOB, and CFR shipments pass freight through at current rates, per management. Red Sea routing has added transit time.

qa_highlights.question: How has the Middle East disruption affected sourcing, freight and customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material supply has been uninterrupted through contracts with suppliers, with some added transit time. Sales to Africa, the US and Europe are unaffected, and only the Middle East route is affected. Export is about 45% of revenue and domestic about 54%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin and can it reach the FY23 peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims to maintain about 6% consolidated EBITDA margin and will try to improve, but gave no numeric target for the 7-8% FY22-23 levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and capex headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: India plants ran at about 125-126% of 2-shift nameplate capacity, with 3-shift use in some months. Group utilisation is about 93%. Capex plans are to be drawn up over the next 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the realisations by product and the margin per kL?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 average realisation was INR76,526 per kL across products; PHPO was about INR78,000 per kL. FY26 EBITDA was INR8,696 per kL, and Q4 gross margin spread was INR9,351 per kL.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company handle the cash needs of planned expansion and South Africa?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is debt-free standalone and has reserves and surplus of about INR1,200 crore (clarified from INR1,500 crore). Management said operating cash flow of INR127 crore could fund an expansion of about INR100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can costs be passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin improved through the year, which shows that price increases have been passed on. It said price increases are passed on to customers via contracts and repricing.

544029|2026-06.headline: Gandhar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 92% YoY to INR 1,732 crore and PAT hit a record INR 206 crore on a per-kilolitre spread of INR 28,145.
544029|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose about 92% YoY to INR 1,732 crore and EBITDA reached INR 281 crore, with margin at 16.2% versus 5.1% a year earlier. PAT of INR 206 crore was the company's highest quarterly profit and exceeded the full FY26 profit, per management. Management attributed the spread expansion to exceptional Middle East-driven market conditions, sourcing from domestic base oil producers and higher realisations, and said it expects margins to stay near these levels for one to two quarters. Volume grew about 8% YoY to roughly 131,000 KL, and an interim dividend of 100% of face value was declared.

segments.name: PHPO (personal care, healthcare, pharma, performance oil)
segments.commentary: Primary growth engine with 18% YoY growth, driven by volume and wider revenue from existing customers. Management expects it to remain the star segment and indicated it stays above about 50% of total sales.

segments.name: PIO (process and insulating oil / transformer oil)
segments.commentary: Grew 28% YoY; management said PIO manufacturing volume rose from 14,000 KL to 18,000 KL. Demand from transformer, power and rubber customers; growth expected to be strong going forward.

segments.name: Lubricants
segments.commentary: Broadly stable, described as a resilient revenue base. Price increase taken in automotive lubricants with some delay due to the dealer-distributor network.

segments.name: Texol (Hamriyah Free Zone, Sharjah subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Operations temporarily hit by regional supply constraints and vessel disruptions in Q1; logistics gradually normalising. Management calls it strategically important and margin-accretive. Borrowings sit here, mostly working-capital plus some term loan.

guidance_outlook: Management is hopeful margins stay at or around current levels for most of FY27, and anticipates stellar levels for at least the next 1-2 quarters; said it is not reverting immediately.
Volume growth target of 8-10% (up to 11%) for FY27; management said revenue growth from value would also be higher.
Exports expected to hold at roughly the current share level; the company is aiming to increase export metrics over the year.
Capex plans to be announced in about the next quarter; company says internal accruals can fund capex without term loans, with term loans possible if needed.

Capex plans not yet announced; management is drawing them up and will update in about the next quarter.
Management said it has a debt-free standalone balance sheet and sufficient internal accruals for own-funded capex.
demand_pricing: Price increases were taken across PHPO, PIO and lubricants (automotive lubricants with a lag), per management.
Management attributed the spread to a mix of higher demand, higher realisations and agile raw material sourcing, and said sourcing was the bigger contributor in some answers.
Main base oil supply was from Saudi Arabia and South Korea; Hormuz disruption delayed Saudi shipments, so the company bought more from South Korea and domestic base oil producers at different prices.
Export realisations are about 5-6% higher than domestic realisations, per management.
Management estimates customer stocking of roughly 10-15% at most in the quarter, not a doubling.
Industry growth cited at 5%+ CAGR (CRISIL report) and 6-7% CAGR in a later answer; company has over 4,000 customers and exports to 100+ countries.
Channel partner volumes fluctuate and are not tracked to end industry; PIO is tender-based.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion came from product mix versus inventory gains, and what is the full-year margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory gains were minimal (raw material held 30-40 days); gains came mainly from higher selling prices. It is hopeful margins stay at or near current levels for most of the year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the volume and revenue growth expectations for FY27, and the export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 8-10%, up to 11%, historically; value growth expected to be higher. Exports expected to remain at current levels, with an aim to grow export metrics.

qa_highlights.question: Is the spread sustainable, and what was the gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects margins at stellar levels for at least 1-2 quarters and will not revert immediately. Consolidated gross margin for the quarter was 21.4%. It declined to give forward guidance on the INR 28,000 spread.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PIO and channel partner volumes appear to decline YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel partner volumes are lumpy and not tied to end industry. PIO manufacturing volume rose from 14,000 KL to 18,000 KL on a consolidated basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the borrowing position and trade payables outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone company is debt-free; borrowings are at Texol, mainly working capital plus declining term loan. Trade payables rose from INR 315 crore to INR 430 crore; about INR 600 crore of the INR 900-odd crore payables is not yet due and about 90% is within 90 days, with no rise in payable days.

qa_highlights.question: What are the tax rate and blended margin expectations for FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: India tax rate 25%; blended rate of roughly 23-24% implied. Management declined to give a sustainable margin run-rate beyond the current quarters.

risks_watch: Spread of INR 28,145/KL is far above the INR 8,274/KL normal level; management itself said it should be viewed in the context of exceptional conditions, and historical EBITDA margins were about 5-8%.

Management repeatedly declined to guide on sustainable margin beyond 1-2 quarters or on the spread; watch Q2 FY27 spread and realisations.

Receivables rose with revenue; watch working capital and Texol throughput as logistics normalise.
South Africa entry strategy not yet defined; revenue potential from Indonesia, Europe, USA and South Africa not quantified.
Customer concentration not disclosed; management said top-5 share is not significant across 4,000+ customers.

544030|2026-03.headline: Flair Writing Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8.4% to INR322.9 crore, FY26 revenue up 15.8% to INR1,250.1 crore; crude-linked raw material costs now a margin headwind in Q1 FY27.

Q4 revenue grew 8.4% to INR322.9 crore, with gross margin up 258 bps to 51.2% and EBITDA margin up 217 bps to 17.9%. Own-brand sales reached 91% of revenue, while OEM sales fell, and Creative and Steel Bottles & Houseware together reached 31% of revenue. Management flagged that crude-derivative raw material costs (about 35% of raw materials) rose sharply due to the West Asia crisis, with an expected ~4% margin hit in Q1 FY27 and ~1% by year-end, and retained 15% FY27 revenue guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Pens given it grew ~2% vs high-single-digit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets ~5% annual Pens growth, ~50% for Creative and ~40% for Steel Bottles, with overall growth around 15% and mix of Creative and Steel rising to ~15% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did steel bottle revenue moderate QoQ?

qa_highlights.answer: Maximum ~4% impact in Q1 FY27, easing over three quarters to ~1% by year-end FY27; longer if conflict persists, with pricing actions needed to pass through costs.

qa_highlights.question: Peak revenue potential from existing and planned capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Around INR1,750 crore of sales from the facilities being built, including Valsad; asset-light model not under consideration.

qa_highlights.answer: Machinery is fungible across entities; product allocation across Daman, Valsad, Dehradun and Surat drives standalone vs subsidiary profit. Management points to consolidated numbers as the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost trend versus gross profit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost plus job work is 20-21% of consolidated revenue and stable; other expenses declining as a percentage of sales.

Pens revenue growth of ~2% in FY26 versus high-single-digit earlier guidance; new 5% target to be tracked.

544030|2026-06.headline: Flair Writing Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10.6% YoY to INR319.2 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 16.7% on raw material inflation; FY27 15% growth guidance reiterated.
544030|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 10.6% YoY to INR319.2 crore while gross margin held at 50% (down 31 bps YoY, down 151 bps QoQ). EBITDA rose 7.7% YoY to INR53.3 crore with margin of 16.7% (down 46 bps YoY), and PAT grew only 0.5% YoY to INR29.1 crore as other income fell. Management attributed margin pressure to West Asia-driven raw material inflation, and said price hikes, reduced schemes and discounts are working to offset it. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% and an EBITDA margin target of 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~150 bps QoQ gross margin decline sustainable, and can gross margins stay at these levels over the next 2-3 quarters given polymer price moves?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 FY26 margins were protected by cheaper earlier-procured inventory; raw material inflation hit from Q1 FY27. Price hikes, lower schemes and discounts limited the QoQ gross margin decline to 150 bps. Cost pressure is expected to ease over the next three quarters, with an EBITDA margin target of 17-18% for the year. Q1 impact was about 1.5% from input costs, against an earlier 100-200 bps estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Pens grew 9% versus the ~5% CAGR guided last quarter, while Creatives grew 23% against the ~50% signalled. What went wrong in Creatives?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohit Rathod said nothing went wrong. Creatives growth was held back by deliberate volume-versus-margin trade-offs in geometry boxes, pencils and some colouring sub-categories. Pens growth was driven by Flair and Hauser brand pull, and the company said it had previously guided to high single digit. Revenue guidance of 15% was reiterated.

qa_highlights.question: Steel Bottles: current utilisation, potential revenue from existing lines, and the new line's timing and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 65%; management invests in new capacity once utilisation crosses 65-75%. The fourth line costs about INR15 crore, adds about 35% capacity and is expected to generate INR30-35 crore revenue depending on product mix. Existing lines can support about INR100 crore revenue at current capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company hit 15% FY27 growth, which implies about 18% growth for the rest of the year, and is top-line growth accelerating?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is sticking to the 15% guidance based on domestic and export demand. Pens are expected to grow high single digit, while Creatives and Steel Bottles are expected to grow about 40%. Alpesh Porwal said 15% CAGR over three years is easily achievable, but declined to give a higher number.

qa_highlights.question: How do the Valsad and Surat capacity additions and the Creative capacity (reported at 75% utilisation) support growth, and when will they be ready?
qa_highlights.answer: Valsad building is capitalised; machinery and moulds are yet to be installed, with commissioning around end of Q1 and full utilisation over the next two quarters. Capex to revenue is about 3x, covering about 1.5 years of growth for Pens and Creatives. Surat has begun 100% operations in the new factory.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and inventory outlook, and the impact of the new ERP system?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital days improved 6 days YoY and were stable QoQ. Management expects about 10 days improvement by end FY27 as inventory normalises after higher raw material stocks held during the crisis. The ERP is expected to be fully operational within 2-3 months, with inventory benefits to follow.

EBITDA margin compressed to 12.3% from 17.6%, mainly from roughly 400 bps gross margin decline due to West Asia-linked raw material inflation (about 20% average RM price rise in Q1), plus ESOP, new-facility and channel partner event costs. PAT fell to INR45.3 crore from INR59.1 crore, with PAT margin at 6.8% versus 10.5%. Management chose volume and market share over near-term margin, calls the margin dip temporary, and gave limited visibility on margins given fluctuating raw material costs.
